You'll join our Public Sector & Charities team as a Research Executive, working on research that helps government departments, charities, academics and NGOs understand public attitudes and make informed decisions. You'll contribute to projects from questionnaire design and data analysis through to reporting and presenting findings to clients, working across a wide variety of social and public-policy topics.

Depending on your experience, you'll manage some projects independently and work alongside senior researchers on larger or more complex studies. We're looking for someone who combines strong quantitative and communication skills with curiosity, initiative, and excellent attention to detail.

Responsibilities

Manage research projects from start to finish, with support from senior colleagues, ensuring projects are delivered to a high standard. Help design questionnaires and surveys, translating clients' research objectives into clear, unbiased, and effective questions. Analyse and interpret quantitative data, identifying the findings and insights that explain why the results matter. Work directly with clients and colleagues throughout projects, communicating clearly and ensuring the research meets the brief. Take ownership of the quality of your work, proactively checking outputs, spotting potential issues, and finding solutions. Contribute positively to the wider team, building strong working relationships and supporting colleagues where needed. 

Behavioural Competencies

Strong critical thinking and curiosity: you enjoy interrogating information, spotting inconsistencies, and working out what findings really mean. Initiative and ownership: you're comfortable getting started independently, anticipating what needs to happen next, and finding solutions to problems. Excellent attention to detail: you check your own work carefully and care about getting things right. Strong organisation: you can manage competing tasks, meet deadlines, and communicate early when something needs attention. Clear communication: you can explain ideas and findings accurately and simply, both in writing and verbally. Confidence with numbers: you're comfortable working with quantitative information and are interested in developing your research skills. 

Qualifications

Experience of contributing to research projects, including evidence you can take ownership, learn quickly, and provide high quality work. Up to 1 years’ relevant experience, gained at a research agency or a mix of agency and client-side. An existing understanding of quantitative research is desirable, while confidence working with data is essential. Degree-level education or equivalent experience; a research, social science or related qualification such as the MRS Advanced Certificate would be an advantage. 

Candidates must submit a 1 page Cover Letter with their application stating why their skills and experience make them a great fit for the position and highlighting relevant achievements.

As part of our application process, you may be invited to a structured conversation with Zee, an AI interviewer from our partner Zeeda, at a time that suits you. It's a chance to tell us about your experience in your own words, beyond your CV, and every application is reviewed by YouGov, who make all hiring decisions. If you are selected for a conversation with Zee, the invitation will cover how to prepare, how your data is handled and your choices.

Why join YouGov?

Join our global team to help us achieve our social mission: to make millions of people’s opinions heard for the benefit of our local, national, and international communities.

Understanding diversity of opinion requires diversity of background. Although our global panel of millions of people worldwide powers our research, our biggest asset is our people. If our research is to be truly representative of what the world thinks, we need people from all walks of life to be part of the team to bring their perspective to the work we do.

Life at YouGov

We are driven by a set of shared values. We are fast, fearless, and innovative. We work diligently to get it right. We are guided by accuracy, ethics, and proven methodologies. We respect and trust each other, bringing these values into everything that we do.

We strive to provide YouGovers with best-in-class benefits to support their physical, financial, and emotional wellbeing. We want our employees to have a sense of belonging and uniqueness in a supportive workplace, so they can bring their full selves to work.

Equal Opportunity Employer

As an Equal Opportunity Employer, qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, gender identity or expression, and sexual orientation), parental status, national origin, marital status, age, disability, genetic information, HIV status, political affiliation, socioeconomic background, veteran status or any other characteristic protected by law or in line with our responsibilities as a fair and ethic employer. All employment decisions are made based on occupational qualifications, merit, and business need.

Data Privacy

To find out how we collect and use your personal data when you apply for a role at YouGov, please read our privacy notice at https://jobs.yougov.com/privacy

rows.title: Pricing Executive
rows.descriptionText:
Who we are 🌍

We’re IAG Loyalty - one organisation with two ambitious, growing divisions across Loyalty and Holidays. Each has its own goals, strategy and team, but together we’re united by a shared vision to create a more rewarding world of travel and experiences.

Our Loyalty division is home to Avios, the global loyalty currency, enabling millions of members to collect and spend rewards across travel, retail and financial services.

Our Holidays division including British Airways Holidays and Iberia Vacaciones, brings together trusted brands, connecting customers to thousands of destinations worldwide through seamless, end-to-end travel experiences.

We’re on an exciting journey of growth and transformation – we’re going places.

The opportunity ✨

If you're looking for a role where you can develop your analytical skills, work on interesting commercial challenges and be part of a supportive team, this could be the perfect next step.

We're looking for two Pricing Executives to join our collaborative Pricing team. One permanent opportunity and one 12-month fixed-term contract.

You'll use data to answer commercial questions and help shape the way customers use Avios. Avios helps millions of people turn everyday spending and travel into rewarding experiences by allowing them to collect and spend points on flights, upgrades, holidays and more. By analysing customer behaviour, demand, redemption trends and pricing performance, you'll uncover insights that help inform pricing decisions, customer propositions and promotions across our Loyalty business.

You'll work with some of the world's best-known airlines on a wide variety of projects, from reward flights and pricing initiatives to new customer propositions. It's a role where you'll see how your analysis helps inform decisions that millions of customers experience.

You'll also be joining a genuinely collaborative team. You'll work closely with experienced analysts, sharing ideas, solving problems together and learning from one another every day. At the same time, you'll be trusted to take ownership of your own work, giving you the opportunity to build confidence while developing your technical and commercial skills.

There are lots of places you could continue your career in analytics. This role is all about curiosity, teamwork and using data to solve a variety of commercial challenges, so you'll get the most from it if you enjoy asking questions, sharing ideas and learning from others.

You don't need experience in the travel or loyalty industry. If you're excited by the idea of using data to solve real business problems and want to continue developing your analytical skills, we'd love to hear from you.

This role is all about curiosity, teamwork and using data to solve a variety of commercial challenges, so you'll get the most from it if you enjoy asking questions, sharing ideas and learning from others.

What you'll be doing 🚀

Support the development and optimisation of pricing strategies across Reward Flights, Pay with Avios and related loyalty redemption products. Write and optimise SQL queries to explore and combine data from multiple sources. Analyse data using tools including Tableau, Astrato and Excel to identify trends, opportunities and answer commercial questions. Build, own and maintain reports and dashboards, along with presentations that bring data to life to inform tactical and strategic pricing decisions. You’ll play a key role in ensuring our pricing approaches are data-driven, efficient and aligned to business targets.  Work closely with colleagues across Commercial, Marketing, Finance, Data and Revenue Management, as well as airline partners. Explore how AI can support more effective and efficient ways of working. 

What we need from you ⚡

You'll Be Someone Who Has

Proficiency in SQL for data extraction, analysis and reporting through education or a previous role. Strong analytical, numerical and commercial acumen.  Experience working with large datasets from multiple sources.  High attention to detail and a strong commitment to data accuracy and integrity.  Strong communication skills with the ability to explain complex data clearly and confidently.  Experience working with dashboards and reporting tools (e.g. Tableau, Power BI or similar).  Confidence engaging with stakeholders at different levels, including senior audiences.  An innovative mindset with curiosity, urgency and a desire to continuously improve ways of working.  Ability to manage multiple priorities, work independently and take ownership of deliverables.  Collaborative approach with strong relationship-building skills across teams.  Is curious about AI and interested in how it can support analysis. 

The Blend 📍 

This role is based in our London office in our Loyalty division.

We call our approach to hybrid working The Blend—it's about giving you the flexibility to choose where you do your best work while staying connected with your team and the wider business.

You'll spend at least two days each week in the office, with the rest of your time working from home. Depending on your role and priorities, you may also work from one of our other offices or partner locations.

We Might Not Be Right For You If

You prefer a role with the same routine every day or enjoy working independently with limited collaboration. This role is all about curiosity, teamwork and using data to solve a variety of commercial challenges, so you'll get the most from it if you enjoy asking questions, sharing ideas and learning from others. 

Diversity and Inclusion 

Our vision is to create a more rewarding world of travel and experiences. Delivering that requires diverse thinking and inclusive leadership.

We are committed to building a workplace where people feel they belong and are valued for their perspective. Inclusion drives better decisions, stronger performance and more innovative outcomes.

We actively encourage applications from people with different experiences and backgrounds, and are committed to ensuring our recruitment process is fair, inclusive and accessible.

rows.title: Data Analyst
rows.descriptionText:
This is a rare opportunity to join a high-performing Policy team, working with 24 leading UK universities. We’re looking for an outstanding Data Analyst to provide analytical and data visualisation support for our policy development and advocacy work.
Through collaboration and advocacy, the Russell Group works to advance and champion the positive economic, societal and cultural contributions of our universities. The Russell Group represents the interests of our 24 university members at the highest level of government, as well as with key research and innovation funders, with business, third-sector partners, regulators, and internationally with like-minded bodies.
As Data Analyst, you will provide robust, clear and timely analysis of a wide range of higher education and research datasets to support the Russell Group’s policy and advocacy positions. This is a new role in the organisation to increase our data analytical capability, supporting the work of colleagues across the Strategic Policy and External Relations teams.
The role involves, but is not limited to, the following:
Undertaking regular and timely analysis of official datasets relevant to the Russell Group including:Higher Education datasets published by UCAS, HESA, OfS and DfE.Research and Innovation datasets published by HESA, UKRI, and DBIST.Datasets relevant to the international team including the CORDIS Horizon Europe Dataset and Home Office migration statistics
Providing data analytical support across the organisation including to colleagues in the Strategic Policy and External Relations teams. This will include:
Working with the Senior Data Manager to quality assure internal data and analysis across the organisation.
Assessing and critiquing ad hoc data presented in media articles, academic publications and think tank reports.
Providing high quality briefings in writing and in person for internal and external parties on data relating to higher education and research.
Creating effective data visualisations to support analysis, storytelling and advocacy, tailoring outputs appropriately for internal colleagues and Russell Group members, as well as political, media and other external stakeholder audiences.
Ensuring that Russell Group policy and external engagement work is informed by an awareness and thorough understanding of relevant data.
Working with the Senior Data Manager to enhance the overall competency within the Russell Group to use data effectively for policy and communications purposes.
Managing data in accordance with the Russell Group's data protection policies.
You will also be responsible for delivering any additional responsibilities, at the request of the Director of Strategic Policy, in accordance with your experience and the broad purpose of this role.
Candidates will need to be able to demonstrate the following:
Keen attention to detail and strong analytical skills, including the ability to undertake statistical analysis. Being an expert user of Excel, including the use of pivot tables, is essential.
Substantial experience analysing large and complex data sets. Ideally with direct experience of working with the higher education and research datasets described above.
Experience of using data to inform policy analysis/development and to underpin impactful advocacy.
The ability to exercise excellent judgement on the confidence of particular data analysis outputs and be able to advise Strategic Policy and External Relations colleagues on the limitations of available datasets and how to use data in ways which are proportionate, robust and not misleading.
Experience of presenting and explaining data outcomes to a range of audiences including internal and external stakeholders, and communicating complex findings clearly and succinctly.
Experience of selecting and creating appropriate visual formats to communicate complex data clearly, including charts, dashboards, infographics and other accessible formats for non-specialist audiences.
The ability to work in an agile way in a fast-paced environment, managing and prioritising a challenging and varied portfolio of work to meet tight deadlines. A flexible, collegiate and cooperative approach to working is essential.
An interest in and knowledge of the higher education policy landscape would also be desirable.
Our Candidate Pack, which includes the vacancy description for the role, and our Equal Opportunities Monitoring form are available to download from the Russell Group Careers site (https://russellgroup-ac-uk.pinpointhq.com/)
Our offices are based in the heart of Westminster, with proximity to key stakeholders and easy access to public transport links. To maximise effective team-based working, we offer flexibility for staff to work from home up to two days a week, subject to work priorities. Benefits include:
Membership of the USS pension scheme25 days of Annual Leave at start, increasing by 1 day annually to a maximum of 30 daysDiscretionary closure days at Easter and Christmas holidays (in addition to Public Holidays)Private healthcare insuranceEmployee Assistance Programme
The starting salary will be in the range of £40,000-£45,000. This is dependent on skills and experience. A higher salary may be available for exceptional and highly experienced candidates.
Closing date for all applications: 17:00 on Wednesday, 28 October 2026
To apply, please visit our Careers site (https://russellgroup-ac-uk.pinpointhq.com/) and submit the following by the closing date:
1) An up-to-date curriculum vitae (max. two sides of A4) including:details of your current and past employmentyour degree qualifications including subjects and gradesa reference from your current or most recent employer
2) A cover letter no more than two sides of A4 addressing the following points:how your knowledge, skills and experience meet the requirements of the rolewhy you are interested in working for the Russell Group
3) We ask all applicants to complete an Equal Opportunities Monitoring form which you can download from our Careers site.
Further information on the Russell Group can be found at https://www.russellgroup.ac.uk/

rows.title: Data Analyst - Participant Support Operations & Clinical Operations
rows.descriptionText:
We have an exciting opportunity for a Data Analyst to join our Analytics team, using data and operational insight to help improve both the participant experience and the journey of biosamples through our study.You'll work closely with operational and technical teams to understand performance, investigate complex problems and turn data into practical recommendations. From understanding participant contact volumes and service demand to identifying bottlenecks across biosample logistics, your analysis will help teams make better decisions, improve processes and deliver more efficient and reliable operations.Despite big improvements in healthcare in our lifetimes, today millions of people in the UK still live in poor health as they get older. Diseases like cancer, dementia, diabetes, and heart disease affect the lives of many people in our communities. Our goal is to create a world-leading resource for health research, to improve our understanding and spot the patterns of how and why common diseases start, so treatments can begin sooner and be more effective.Our Future Health will be the UK's largest ever health research programme, bringing people together to develop new ways to detect, prevent, and treat diseases. We are a charity, supported by the UK Government, in partnership with charities and industry. We work closely with the NHS and with public authorities across all nations and regions of the UK.What you'll be doing:In this role, you'll partner with teams across Participant Support Operations, Clinical Operations and Analytics to solve operational problems using data and evidence. You'll develop trusted reporting and metrics, investigate issues across multiple systems and help teams move towards more proactive, data-informed performance management.Your key responsibilities will include but not be limited to:Analyse participant contact volumes, service performance, complaints and backlogs, using forecasting and capacity planning to help teams understand and manage demandIdentify trends and drivers within participant enquiries and complaints, turning your findings into actionable recommendations to improve participant experience and operational efficiencyAnalyse the end-to-end biosample journey across operational, logistics and laboratory systems, identifying delays, discrepancies, anomalies and quality issuesUse SQL and exploratory analysis to investigate data across multiple systems, reconstruct operational workflows and identify the root causes of issuesDevelop and maintain operational reporting, performance metrics and monitoring across participant support and biosample operationsWork with Analytics Engineers, Data Scientists and operational teams to improve data quality, traceability and reporting capabilityTranslate operational questions into structured analytical approaches and communicate findings clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholdersHelp teams move from manual and reactive reporting towards proactive performance management and data-informed decision-makingYou'll be part of a wider Analytics function made up of analysts, data scientists and data engineers. The team works remotely, coming together in person twice a month for collaboration and co-working, as well as quarterly strategy days focused on planning, problem-solving and longer-term thinking. We also have a regular book club and team demos, which give us space to learn together and celebrate what we're building. 
Hiring Process We feel hiring should be transparent and give you a real sense for what Our Future Health is like. Here's what you can expect: Initial chat with our Talent team (30 min) to get to know each other, discuss the role, and answer any questions you have1st interview with our Analytics Manager (25 min) - this is an opportunity to meet your potential line manager and for you both to align on role expectationsTechnical interview with 2-3 members from our Analytics team (60 min). This will include a short task you'll need to prepare in advance of the interview and is designed to get a sense for how you'd approach the real-world responsibilities of this roleFinal stage competency interview (60 min) with a small cross-functional panel of your potential new stakeholders. This will focus on how you collaborate, work with stakeholders, and navigate ambiguity and challenges in real-world projects

Requirements

We recognise that candidates may have developed relevant experience through different career paths and welcome applications from those who can demonstrate many, though not necessarily all, of the skills and experience listed below:Strong SQL skills and experience working with relational databases and cloud data platforms such as SnowflakeExperience analysing complex operational data from multiple systems and investigating data quality issues, discrepancies and operational risksExperience developing and maintaining reporting, dashboards, datasets or other analytical products used by operational teamsAn understanding of operational performance analysis, which could have been developed within areas such as healthcare, logistics, customer operations, participant services, research or another complex operational environmentFamiliarity with data modelling concepts and experience collaborating with Analytics Engineering or Data Engineering teamsStrong problem-solving skills, with the ability to investigate root causes and turn analysis into practical recommendationsThe ability to communicate complex analytical findings clearly and build effective relationships with both operational and technical stakeholdersAn organised and adaptable approach, with the ability to manage competing priorities while maintaining a high level of accuracy and attention to data qualityKnowledge of forecasting, capacity planning, performance measurement or operational analytics methodologies would be advantageousAn understanding of statistical concepts and performance monitoring techniques, such as variation analysis or statistical process control, would be beneficialExperience using Python or R for data manipulation, analysis, automation or exploratory investigation would also be beneficial. 

Benefits

From £53,000 annum basic salary.Generous Pension Scheme - We invest in your future with employer contributions of up to 12%30 Days Holiday + Bank Holidays - Enjoy a generous holiday allowance with the flexibility to take bank holidays when it suits youEnhanced Parental Leave - Supporting you during life's biggest momentsCycle to Work Scheme - Save 25-39% on a new bike and accessories through salary sacrificeHome & Tech Savings - Get up to 8% off on IKEA and Currys products, spreading the cost over 12 months through salary sacrifice£1,000 Employee Referral Bonus - Know someone amazing? Get rewarded for bringing them on board!Wellbeing Support - Access to Mental Health First Aiders, plus 24/7 online GP services and an Employee Assistance Programme for you and your familyA Great Place to Work - We have a lovely Central London office in Holborn, and offer flexible and remote working arrangementsJoin us - let's prevent disease together.Closing date: 12 October 2026 at 5:00 pmWe may close this vacancy earlier than the advertised closing date if we receive a high volume of applications, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.At Our Future Health, we recognise the importance of having a diverse workforce and ensuring that all candidates, regardless of their background, have equitable access to our application process. We proactively encourage applicants who identify as having a disability, neurodiversity, or long-term health conditions to let us know if they require any reasonable adjustments as part of their application process.If you do require any reasonable adjustments, please email us at talent@ourfuturehealth.org.uk.

rows.title: Data Analyst Intern (TikTok-LIVE) - 2027 Start
rows.descriptionText:
Responsibilities

About the Team

The Regional LIVE Operation Strategy Team leads various cross-functional projects. Our key initiatives include developing strategic plans to drive widespread adoption of LIVE at scale among creators, localising new product features, creating user engagement strategies, ensuring a positive creator experience through education on the Community Guidelines and best practices, and providing ad hoc analysis and support to cross-functional partners.

We are looking for talented individuals to join us for an internship. Our internship program offers students hands-on experience, industry exposure, and opportunities to apply their knowledge to real-world challenges while building a strong foundation for personal and professional growth.

Interns will gain practical experience, explore potential career paths, and participate in social events, learning programs, and development workshops alongside industry professionals.

Candidates may apply to a maximum of two positions across Our Company and its affiliates globally. Applications will be considered in the order they are submitted.

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, so we encourage you to apply early. Please clearly state your availability in your resume, including your start and end dates.

Internship Overview

We're looking for a Data Analyst project intern to join our dynamic LIVE team. In this role, you’ll uncover insights and deliver data-driven recommendations that directly impact how we grow and support our creator ecosystem. You'll work cross-functionally with product, strategy, and operations teams to shape our growth priorities using data and analytical thinking.

As a project intern, you will have the opportunity to engage in impactful short-mid term projects that provide you with a glimpse of professional real-world experience. You will gain practical skills through on-the-job learning in a fast-paced work environment and develop a deeper understanding of your career interests.

Examples Of Problems You’ll Be Solving

 What are the best content verticals for us to focus our creator recruitment on? How can we build a predictive model to identify high-potential creators early? What are the right leading and lagging indicators to measure success against our key OKRs? How can we segment creators and users to better personalise support and growth strategies? When and how should we educate creators to maximise their long-term retention and performance? How can we simplify complex data sets using statistical tools to better diagnose issues and recommend scalable solutions?

Key Responsibilities

 Analyse local and global content and user trends to identify growth opportunities within the EU LIVE ecosystem. Participate in the growth and exploration of future AI implementation and direction and be responsible for the data analysis of core business modules. Create, automate, and maintain reports and dashboards to track performance, OKRs, and key strategic initiatives. Develop data models and perform in-depth analyses to support content strategy, creator segmentation, and user engagement. Translate complex data into actionable insights for regional teams and leadership. Collaborate closely with cross-functional teams (e.g., Creator Management, Product, Strategy) to inform decision-making. Present findings clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders to influence business strategy.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications

 Currently pursuing an Undergraduate degree in Statistics, Engineering, Economics, or a related quantitative discipline. Experience with SQL, Python or another related programming language To succeed in the role, you need to be a proactive, self-driven and impact driven person Be able to work with cross-functional teams in a fast speed environment Demonstrated ability to communicate findings clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences Comfortable working with large datasets and drawing actionable conclusions under ambiguity Fast learner with the ability to quickly grasp new tools, concepts, and workflows, then apply them effectively to practical business problems Strong analytical thinking and ability to turn ambiguous business questions into structured analysis

Preferred Qualifications

 Experience with visualisation platforms (Tableau, Looker, Power BI) and narrative based story telling with data is a plus Social Media content creation experience and familiarity with live-streaming platforms is strongly preferred Familiarity with statistical concepts such as segmentation, regression, or predictive modelling Previous internship, academic project, or work experience involving data analysis or business analytics Exposure to A/B testing or experimentation frameworks Familiarity with OKR frameworks or performance metric design

Job Information

About TikTok

TikTok is the leading destination for short-form mobile video. At TikTok, our mission is to inspire creativity and bring joy. TikTok's global headquarters are in Los Angeles and Singapore, and we also have offices in New York City, London, Dublin, Paris, Berlin, Dubai, Jakarta, Seoul, and Tokyo.

Why Join Us

Inspiring creativity is at the core of TikTok's mission. Our innovative product is built to help people authentically express themselves, discover and connect – and our global, diverse teams make that possible. Together, we create value for our communities, inspire creativity and bring joy - a mission we work towards every day.

We strive to do great things with great people. We lead with curiosity, humility, and a desire to make impact in a rapidly growing tech company. Every challenge is an opportunity to learn and innovate as one team. We're resilient and embrace challenges as they come. By constantly iterating and fostering an "Always Day 1" mindset, we achieve meaningful breakthroughs for ourselves, our company, and our users. When we create and grow together, the possibilities are limitless. Join us.

Diversity & Inclusion

TikTok is committed to creating an inclusive space where employees are valued for their skills, experiences, and unique perspectives. Our platform connects people from across the globe and so does our workplace. At TikTok, our mission is to inspire creativity and bring joy. To achieve that goal, we are committed to celebrating our diverse voices and to creating an environment that reflects the many communities we reach. We are passionate about this and hope you are too.

rows.descriptionText:
Welcome to Hastings Direct

We’re a digital insurance provider with a clear strategy to become the best and biggest player in the UK market. As a company, we’ve made huge investments in our technology, pricing, data and analytics capabilities over the past few years, along with nurturing our 4Cs culture and substantial investment in our people. And as a Finance team, we're doing exactly the same – building a market leading finance technology platform, investing in our team and our approach to leadership development, with a real focus on commercially adding value to the business.

The fact you’re now reading this job advert means we’ve tempted you to find out more about . If you like what you see, we hope you'll consider joining our team.

We have high standards and understand some people may not apply for jobs unless they feel they tick every box. If you’re excited about joining us and think you have some of what we are looking for, even if you’re not 100% sure, we would love to hear from you.

Job Title: Data Scientist

Location: Bexhill/Leicester/London – Hybrid

Unfortunately, we are unable to offer sponsorship for this position

Role Purpose 

The Data Scientist will assist in the design, development, and deployment of predictive models that feed into Hastings’ market-leading pricing activities. This role is within a team of Data Scientists championing machine learning (ML) techniques to improve predictive performance using vast amounts of customer information.  

Accountabilities 

Your responsibilities will include: 

Develop and support predictive models to assess insurance risk and inform pricing and underwriting decisions.Contribute to the integration of models into production systems and support their ongoing monitoring and maintenance.Develop, maintain and improve reusable tools, pipelines and processes that enable efficient, reliable and reproducible modelling, following agreed standards for coding, documentation, testing and model development.Identify, assess and prepare new data features, evaluating their predictive value, stability, interpretability and potential impact on customer pricing outcomes.

Skills, Knowledge & Experience 

Essential 

Experience building and evaluating predictive models such as linear and gradient boosted models.Proficiency using Python and appropriate machine-learning libraries.Proficiency in SQL, including preparing and transforming data for predictive modelling.Basic knowledge of Git or other code version control systems.Strong communication skills and time management skills.Demonstrable experience delivering data science solutions that have influenced business decisions and generated measurable commercial value.

Desirable

rows.title: Customs Analyst
rows.descriptionText:
About The Role

We are looking for a dedicated compliance professional to join our Waitrose Customs and Excise team who ensure all imported and exported stock is accurately declared to Customs on time. In this role, you will champion regulatory compliance, manage commodity code classification and use of Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) in accordance with Preferential Origin rules. You’ll play a crucial part in maintaining robust audit trails, monitoring UK and Channel Islands customs entries, supporting sustainability reporting, and ensuring we pay the correct duties and VAT.

At a glance

Salary range - Expected Salary up to £45,000, depending on skills and experience

Contract type - This is a permanent position

Working pattern/flexible working - The Partnership has adopted a hybrid working approach, meaning you'll be able to work a mixture between the office and home based upon your personal needs whilst balancing the needs of the business. There is an expectation you will attend the office regularly to connect with the team and on a more ad-hoc basis to attend key meetings as required.

Hours of Work - 35 hours per week

Location - Pimlico, London

Key Responsibilities

Legal Compliance: Make declarations to HMRC through the Customs Declaration Service (CDS), ensuring entries meet all regulatory requirements and are within the correct time period. Adhere to all classification, origin, preference, and valuation legislation across both EU and ROW movements. Maintain operational awareness of the Border Target Operating Model (BTOM) and Windsor Framework.Product Classification & FTAs: Work closely with Buying to identify new products and confirm the correct commodity code to set import duty rates and identify import restrictions. Act as a subject matter expert on Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) to optimise preferential origin sourcing.Risk Management: Establish how to identify and apply relevant rules of origin and valuation rules, ensuring suppliers are aware of their responsibility. Maintain appropriate controls and up-to-date evidential documentation. Assist with Business Control checks, MSS checks, and entry amendments. Raise and escalate areas of concern. Manage returns and deferment accounts appropriately.Reporting & Sustainability Support: Extract, manage, and prepare compliance data to support wider team needs, specifically generating reports required for modern environmental and sustainability tracking.Process Development & Systems: Work proactively to identify opportunities for process improvements. Utilise advanced Google Spreadsheets (including Apps Script) to automate and streamline workflows. Leverage modern tech to boost efficiency.Teamwork, Training & Functional Leadership: Lead the onboarding process for new starters and provide functional leadership on specific compliance tasks. Coordinate work proactively with others to ensure deadlines are met and maintain high service levels.Control use of Deferment and VAT: Help manage the use of our Deferment and EORI numbers through the controlled approval of road, air and courier shipments. Understand when it is appropriate for other deferment accounts to be used. Authorise and manage returned goods with support of the Line Manager

Essential Skills/experience You’ll Need

Proven experience of Customs entries including extensive hands-on experience using the Customs Declaration Service (CDS)Deep knowledge of Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) and both preferential and non-preferential origin rulesStrong knowledge of customs valuation rulesKnowledge of documentation requirements for different products and originsGood written and verbal communication skillsExcellent attention to detailAbility to train and support others (Onboarding Lead)Ability to work under pressure to remain compliant and meet deadlines 

Desirable Skills/experience You May Have

Experience of working in Excise mattersExperience with AI-assisted classification toolsAdvanced proficiency in Google Spreadsheets (including Apps Script)Knowledge of Incoterms and associated risksAdvanced data visualisation skills (e.g., Tableau)

About The Partnership

We’re the largest employee owned business in the UK and home of our cherished brands, John Lewis and Waitrose. We’re not just employees, we’re Partners, driven by our purpose to build a happier world. As we look to our future, there’s never been a more exciting time to join us.

We’re ruthlessly focused on being brilliant at retail. We continue to innovate, adapt and diversify. Never Knowingly Undersold on price, quality and service in John Lewis and passionately serving food-lovers in Waitrose.

As Partners we all share the responsibility of ownership and in its rewards. We use our voices to contribute to our success, working together through the good and challenging times, holding true to our behaviours and treating everyone with kindness and respect.

We all own making the Partnership somewhere we belong. Embracing our differences and creating an environment where we’re free to be ourselves and can THRIVE. Growing ourselves individually, and as a collective.

As Partners, we make all the difference. And, we all own it.

Important points to note: 

It’s important to note that some of our roles are subject to pre-employment vetting (which may include DBS checks for successful candidates). If required, you’ll be informed and provided with information about vetting during the recruitment process and we encourage you to complete any vetting documents quickly to avoid delays. Any DBS checks required will be carried out by a third-party registered body and financial probity checks may also be required for some of our roles.

We occasionally close vacancies early in the event we receive a high volume of applications, and therefore, we recommend you apply early. If you require a reasonable adjustment due to a disability which means you may need longer to complete your application please contact us as soon as possible.

We want all of our Partners to have a good work-life balance and we support flexible working. This might mean flexible or compressed hours, job sharing or shorter hour contracts, where possible. Please discuss this further with the hiring manager during your interview.

rows.title: Product Analyst
rows.descriptionText:
About Dynamo AI
Dynamo AI builds the platform enterprises use to bring AI applications to production and keep them there. Our products cover risk assessment, evaluation, runtime guardrails and observability for generative AI and agentic systems. We work with enterprises in regulated industries, including financial services, insurance, healthcare and defense.
The RoleOur PMs each own a set of business problems, such as getting AI agents approved for production, reducing the effort legal and compliance teams spend on guardrails, or lowering the cost of running guardrails at scale. Almost every one of these problems depends on evidence: whether an approach works, how well, and at what cost. Product Analysts produce that evidence.Working with the PM who owns a problem, you take a specific question within it and own the answer. You scope the question, design the experiment or prototype, define how success is measured, run the analysis, and come back with a recommendation the PM can act on. When building is faster than waiting, that includes standing up a quick tool with AI to test an idea. You may support several PMs as priorities shift.Training and infrastructure code is handled by our engineering and research teams. Your contribution is experimental design, prototyping and analytical rigor.
What You Might Work OnGuardrail creation and upkeep: design and curate the data used to train and accept custom guardrails, keep labeling consistent as datasets grow, and measure whether updates made from production errors improve performance without regressions.Control coverage: benchmark detection against new attack techniques, languages and modalities, and scope what closing each gap would take.Evaluation evidence: assess whether synthetic evaluation and red-teaming data is faithful and diverse enough for customers' approvers to trust, and research new ways to evaluate AI applications and agents.Cost and performance: compare guardrail and orchestration configurations on accuracy, latency and inference cost.Alerting: prototype ways to aggregate and prioritize guardrail alerts, and measure their effect on the workload of security analysts.Workflow prototypes: build and test prototypes of new workflows, such as how legal and compliance reviewers contribute to guardrail policies or how customers onboard an application on their own, and measure the time and effort they take.Rapid tooling: build small custom tools with AI to validate a hypothesis or unblock the team.Benchmarking and reporting: measure performance with standard classification metrics (FNR, FPR, precision, recall) and report what is working and what is not.
Growth PathYou will start on well-scoped questions and move to harder, more ambiguous ones. Over time you will build intuition for SLM training, guardrail orchestration, agent security and how controls fit into a full AI application, along with an understanding of how our customers make approval decisions. This is a track toward a Product Manager or senior technical product role.
RequirementsA degree with strong quantitative or analytical content. We are especially interested in less common backgrounds, such as physics, information or data theory, and business, alongside solid data analysis experience.A clear, demonstrated framework for thinking through problems.Good instincts for data, ML concepts, and what makes an experiment or metric trustworthy.Python and pandas for working with data.Interest in AI security or safety, and in adversarial thinking.Attention to detail and clear writing, including the ability to turn results into a recommendation a PM can act on.
Nice to HaveML coursework, or coursework or projects in statistics or NLP.Reading or working proficiency in Japanese, Chinese or a European language.SQL.A habit of building small tools or scripts, including with AI assistants, to answer your own questions.Exposure to LLMs, AI agents, security tooling, experimental design or annotation work.
Why Join UsProduce the evidence behind product decisions across every Dynamo product.Work on AI security and governance problems that enterprises are facing for the first time.Grow toward a product role at a founder-led startup.Competitive compensation, equity and benefits.

rows.title: Pricing Executive
rows.descriptionText:
Who we are 🌍

We’re IAG Loyalty - one organisation with two ambitious, growing divisions across Loyalty and Holidays. Each has its own goals, strategy and team, but together we’re united by a shared vision to create a more rewarding world of travel and experiences.

Our Loyalty division is home to Avios, the global loyalty currency, enabling millions of members to collect and spend rewards across travel, retail and financial services.

Our Holidays division including British Airways Holidays and Iberia Vacaciones, brings together trusted brands, connecting customers to thousands of destinations worldwide through seamless, end-to-end travel experiences.

We’re on an exciting journey of growth and transformation – we’re going places.

The opportunity ✨

If you're looking for a role where you can develop your analytical skills, work on interesting commercial challenges and be part of a supportive team, this could be the perfect next step.

We're looking for two Pricing Executives to join our collaborative Pricing team. One permanent opportunity and one 12-month fixed-term contract.

You'll use data to answer commercial questions and help shape the way customers use Avios. Avios helps millions of people turn everyday spending and travel into rewarding experiences by allowing them to collect and spend points on flights, upgrades, holidays and more. By analysing customer behaviour, demand, redemption trends and pricing performance, you'll uncover insights that help inform pricing decisions, customer propositions and promotions across our Loyalty business.

You'll work with some of the world's best-known airlines on a wide variety of projects, from reward flights and pricing initiatives to new customer propositions. It's a role where you'll see how your analysis helps inform decisions that millions of customers experience.

You'll also be joining a genuinely collaborative team. You'll work closely with experienced analysts, sharing ideas, solving problems together and learning from one another every day. At the same time, you'll be trusted to take ownership of your own work, giving you the opportunity to build confidence while developing your technical and commercial skills.

There are lots of places you could continue your career in analytics. This role is all about curiosity, teamwork and using data to solve a variety of commercial challenges, so you'll get the most from it if you enjoy asking questions, sharing ideas and learning from others.

You don't need experience in the travel or loyalty industry. If you're excited by the idea of using data to solve real business problems and want to continue developing your analytical skills, we'd love to hear from you.

This role is all about curiosity, teamwork and using data to solve a variety of commercial challenges, so you'll get the most from it if you enjoy asking questions, sharing ideas and learning from others.

What you'll be doing 🚀

Support the development and optimisation of pricing strategies across Reward Flights, Pay with Avios and related loyalty redemption products. Write and optimise SQL queries to explore and combine data from multiple sources. Analyse data using tools including Tableau, Astrato and Excel to identify trends, opportunities and answer commercial questions. Build, own and maintain reports and dashboards, along with presentations that bring data to life to inform tactical and strategic pricing decisions. You’ll play a key role in ensuring our pricing approaches are data-driven, efficient and aligned to business targets.  Work closely with colleagues across Commercial, Marketing, Finance, Data and Revenue Management, as well as airline partners. Explore how AI can support more effective and efficient ways of working. 

What we need from you ⚡

You'll Be Someone Who Has

Proficiency in SQL for data extraction, analysis and reporting through education or a previous role. Strong analytical, numerical and commercial acumen.  Experience working with large datasets from multiple sources.  High attention to detail and a strong commitment to data accuracy and integrity.  Strong communication skills with the ability to explain complex data clearly and confidently.  Experience working with dashboards and reporting tools (e.g. Tableau, Power BI or similar).  Confidence engaging with stakeholders at different levels, including senior audiences.  An innovative mindset with curiosity, urgency and a desire to continuously improve ways of working.  Ability to manage multiple priorities, work independently and take ownership of deliverables.  Collaborative approach with strong relationship-building skills across teams.  Is curious about AI and interested in how it can support analysis. 

The Blend 📍 

This role is based in our London office in our Loyalty division.

We call our approach to hybrid working The Blend—it's about giving you the flexibility to choose where you do your best work while staying connected with your team and the wider business.

You'll spend at least two days each week in the office, with the rest of your time working from home. Depending on your role and priorities, you may also work from one of our other offices or partner locations.

We Might Not Be Right For You If

You prefer a role with the same routine every day or enjoy working independently with limited collaboration. This role is all about curiosity, teamwork and using data to solve a variety of commercial challenges, so you'll get the most from it if you enjoy asking questions, sharing ideas and learning from others. 

Diversity and Inclusion 

Our vision is to create a more rewarding world of travel and experiences. Delivering that requires diverse thinking and inclusive leadership.

We are committed to building a workplace where people feel they belong and are valued for their perspective. Inclusion drives better decisions, stronger performance and more innovative outcomes.

We actively encourage applications from people with different experiences and backgrounds, and are committed to ensuring our recruitment process is fair, inclusive and accessible.

rows.title: Data Analyst - Participant Support Operations & Clinical Operations
rows.descriptionText:
We have an exciting opportunity for a Data Analyst to join our Analytics team, using data and operational insight to help improve both the participant experience and the journey of biosamples through our study.You'll work closely with operational and technical teams to understand performance, investigate complex problems and turn data into practical recommendations. From understanding participant contact volumes and service demand to identifying bottlenecks across biosample logistics, your analysis will help teams make better decisions, improve processes and deliver more efficient and reliable operations.Despite big improvements in healthcare in our lifetimes, today millions of people in the UK still live in poor health as they get older. Diseases like cancer, dementia, diabetes, and heart disease affect the lives of many people in our communities. Our goal is to create a world-leading resource for health research, to improve our understanding and spot the patterns of how and why common diseases start, so treatments can begin sooner and be more effective.Our Future Health will be the UK's largest ever health research programme, bringing people together to develop new ways to detect, prevent, and treat diseases. We are a charity, supported by the UK Government, in partnership with charities and industry. We work closely with the NHS and with public authorities across all nations and regions of the UK.What you'll be doing:In this role, you'll partner with teams across Participant Support Operations, Clinical Operations and Analytics to solve operational problems using data and evidence. You'll develop trusted reporting and metrics, investigate issues across multiple systems and help teams move towards more proactive, data-informed performance management.Your key responsibilities will include but not be limited to:Analyse participant contact volumes, service performance, complaints and backlogs, using forecasting and capacity planning to help teams understand and manage demandIdentify trends and drivers within participant enquiries and complaints, turning your findings into actionable recommendations to improve participant experience and operational efficiencyAnalyse the end-to-end biosample journey across operational, logistics and laboratory systems, identifying delays, discrepancies, anomalies and quality issuesUse SQL and exploratory analysis to investigate data across multiple systems, reconstruct operational workflows and identify the root causes of issuesDevelop and maintain operational reporting, performance metrics and monitoring across participant support and biosample operationsWork with Analytics Engineers, Data Scientists and operational teams to improve data quality, traceability and reporting capabilityTranslate operational questions into structured analytical approaches and communicate findings clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholdersHelp teams move from manual and reactive reporting towards proactive performance management and data-informed decision-makingYou'll be part of a wider Analytics function made up of analysts, data scientists and data engineers. The team works remotely, coming together in person twice a month for collaboration and co-working, as well as quarterly strategy days focused on planning, problem-solving and longer-term thinking. We also have a regular book club and team demos, which give us space to learn together and celebrate what we're building. 
Hiring Process We feel hiring should be transparent and give you a real sense for what Our Future Health is like. Here's what you can expect: Initial chat with our Talent team (30 min) to get to know each other, discuss the role, and answer any questions you have1st interview with our Analytics Manager (25 min) - this is an opportunity to meet your potential line manager and for you both to align on role expectationsTechnical interview with 2-3 members from our Analytics team (60 min). This will include a short task you'll need to prepare in advance of the interview and is designed to get a sense for how you'd approach the real-world responsibilities of this roleFinal stage competency interview (60 min) with a small cross-functional panel of your potential new stakeholders. This will focus on how you collaborate, work with stakeholders, and navigate ambiguity and challenges in real-world projects

Requirements

We recognise that candidates may have developed relevant experience through different career paths and welcome applications from those who can demonstrate many, though not necessarily all, of the skills and experience listed below:Strong SQL skills and experience working with relational databases and cloud data platforms such as SnowflakeExperience analysing complex operational data from multiple systems and investigating data quality issues, discrepancies and operational risksExperience developing and maintaining reporting, dashboards, datasets or other analytical products used by operational teamsAn understanding of operational performance analysis, which could have been developed within areas such as healthcare, logistics, customer operations, participant services, research or another complex operational environmentFamiliarity with data modelling concepts and experience collaborating with Analytics Engineering or Data Engineering teamsStrong problem-solving skills, with the ability to investigate root causes and turn analysis into practical recommendationsThe ability to communicate complex analytical findings clearly and build effective relationships with both operational and technical stakeholdersAn organised and adaptable approach, with the ability to manage competing priorities while maintaining a high level of accuracy and attention to data qualityKnowledge of forecasting, capacity planning, performance measurement or operational analytics methodologies would be advantageousAn understanding of statistical concepts and performance monitoring techniques, such as variation analysis or statistical process control, would be beneficialExperience using Python or R for data manipulation, analysis, automation or exploratory investigation would also be beneficial. 

Benefits

From £53,000 annum basic salary.Generous Pension Scheme - We invest in your future with employer contributions of up to 12%30 Days Holiday + Bank Holidays - Enjoy a generous holiday allowance with the flexibility to take bank holidays when it suits youEnhanced Parental Leave - Supporting you during life's biggest momentsCycle to Work Scheme - Save 25-39% on a new bike and accessories through salary sacrificeHome & Tech Savings - Get up to 8% off on IKEA and Currys products, spreading the cost over 12 months through salary sacrifice£1,000 Employee Referral Bonus - Know someone amazing? Get rewarded for bringing them on board!Wellbeing Support - Access to Mental Health First Aiders, plus 24/7 online GP services and an Employee Assistance Programme for you and your familyA Great Place to Work - We have a lovely Central London office in Holborn, and offer flexible and remote working arrangementsJoin us - let's prevent disease together.Closing date: 12 October 2026 at 5:00 pmWe may close this vacancy earlier than the advertised closing date if we receive a high volume of applications, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.At Our Future Health, we recognise the importance of having a diverse workforce and ensuring that all candidates, regardless of their background, have equitable access to our application process. We proactively encourage applicants who identify as having a disability, neurodiversity, or long-term health conditions to let us know if they require any reasonable adjustments as part of their application process.If you do require any reasonable adjustments, please email us at talent@ourfuturehealth.org.uk.

rows.title: Data Analyst
rows.descriptionText:
About Us

At Trainline, our purpose is to empower greener travel choices, connecting people and places. Trainline enables millions of travellers to find and book the best value tickets across carriers, fares, and journey options through our highly rated mobile app, website, and B2B partner channels.

Great journeys start with Trainline 🚄 

We’re Europe’s leading independent rail platform, helping millions of travellers find and book the best-value rail and coach journeys across our app, website and partner channels.

Our job is to make the green travel choice the best choice. By building a better train travel experience, we help more people choose rail - creating a positive impact for customers, our business and the planet.

We’re a team of more than 1,000 Trainliners from over 50 nationalities, working across London, Paris, Barcelona, Milan, Edinburgh and Madrid. Now is a brilliant time to join us and help shape the future of travel.

Introducing the Trainline Data Analytics Team 👋

Data Analytics is central to how we build better products, support our customers and grow our business. Our Data Analysts are embedded across cross-functional teams spanning product, commercial and industry initiatives, working closely with Product Managers, Software Engineers, Commercial teams, Embedded Data Scientists and the wider Data organisation to enable confident, evidence-based decision making.

As a Data Analyst in the Travel & Disruption team, you will help us build a better travel proposition for our customers. You'll use data to understand how customers engage with our travel features throughout their journey, helping teams make better decisions that improve the travel experience. Whether customers are enjoying a seamless journey or navigating unexpected disruption, your insights will help shape products and services that make rail travel easier, more reliable and more rewarding for millions of customers.

In this role as the Data Analyst, you will...🚄

Analyse customer behaviour in relation to our travel products.Translate complex analysis into clear, compelling insights and practical recommendations for technical and non-technical audiences.Produce high-quality analytical deliverables, dashboards, reports and presentations that help senior stakeholders and external partners make informed decisions.Work closely with Data Scientists to structure analytical approaches, interpret findings and draw meaningful conclusions from large and complex datasets.Collaborate across Data, Product and Design to ensure insight is embedded into decision making from early exploration through to delivery.Help define how we measure success in the Travel space.Contribute to a growing Data organisation that includes Data Science, Machine Learning, Data Engineering, Business Intelligence and Data Product Management.

We'd love to hear from you if you have...🔍

Experience using analytics to support business decisions, answer complex commercial questions and identify opportunities for improvement.Strong SQL skills and confidence working with large datasets to produce accurate, reliable and well-structured analysis.The ability to structure analytical work clearly, navigate ambiguity and turn complex findings into actionable recommendations.Experience communicating insight to a range of audiences, including senior stakeholders and colleagues from technical and non-technical backgrounds.Strong data visualisation skills, ideally using tools such as Tableau, Power BI or similar.A thoughtful approach to storytelling, with the ability to create polished deliverables that make insight easy to understand and act on.Strong organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple analytical work streams and balance competing priorities.Ideally, experience with DBT or modern data transformation workflows, and exposure to analysing experiments, pilots or trials.

More Information

Enjoy fantastic perks like private healthcare & dental insurance, a generous work from abroad policy, 2-for-1 share purchase plans, an EV Scheme to further reduce carbon emissions, extra festive time off, and excellent family-friendly benefits.

We prioritise career growth with clear career paths, transparent pay bands, personal learning budgets, and regular learning days. Jump on board and supercharge your career from day one!

We're operating a hybrid model and ask that Trainliners work from the office a minimum of 60% of their time over a 12-week period. We also have a 28-day Work from Abroad policy.

Our Values Represent The Things That Matter Most To Us And What We Live And Breathe Everyday, In Everything We Do

💭 Think Big - We're building the future of rail ✔️ Own It - We focus on every customer, partner and journey 🤝 Travel Together - We're one team ♻️ Do Good - We make a positive impact 

We know that having a diverse team makes us better and helps us succeed. And we mean all forms of diversity - gender, ethnicity, sexuality, disability, nationality and diversity of thought. That's why we're committed to creating inclusive places to work, where everyone belongs and differences are valued and celebrated.

rows.title: Data Analyst
rows.descriptionText:
About Us

At Trainline, our purpose is to empower greener travel choices, connecting people and places. Trainline enables millions of travellers to find and book the best value tickets across carriers, fares, and journey options through our highly rated mobile app, website, and B2B partner channels.

Great journeys start with Trainline 🚄 

We’re Europe’s leading independent rail platform, helping millions of travellers find and book the best-value rail and coach journeys across our app, website and partner channels.

Our job is to make the green travel choice the best choice. By building a better train travel experience, we help more people choose rail - creating a positive impact for customers, our business and the planet.

We’re a team of more than 1,000 Trainliners from over 50 nationalities, working across London, Paris, Barcelona, Milan, Edinburgh and Madrid. Now is a brilliant time to join us and help shape the future of travel.

Introducing the Trainline Data Analytics Team 👋

Data Analytics is central to how we build better products, support our customers and grow our business. Our Data Analysts are embedded across cross-functional teams spanning product, commercial and industry initiatives, working closely with Product Managers, Software Engineers, Commercial teams, Embedded Data Scientists and the wider Data organisation to enable confident, evidence-based decision making.

As a Data Analyst in the Travel & Disruption team, you will help us build a better travel proposition for our customers. You'll use data to understand how customers engage with our travel features throughout their journey, helping teams make better decisions that improve the travel experience. Whether customers are enjoying a seamless journey or navigating unexpected disruption, your insights will help shape products and services that make rail travel easier, more reliable and more rewarding for millions of customers.

In this role as the Data Analyst, you will...🚄

Analyse customer behaviour in relation to our travel products.Translate complex analysis into clear, compelling insights and practical recommendations for technical and non-technical audiences.Produce high-quality analytical deliverables, dashboards, reports and presentations that help senior stakeholders and external partners make informed decisions.Work closely with Data Scientists to structure analytical approaches, interpret findings and draw meaningful conclusions from large and complex datasets.Collaborate across Data, Product and Design to ensure insight is embedded into decision making from early exploration through to delivery.Help define how we measure success in the Travel space.Contribute to a growing Data organisation that includes Data Science, Machine Learning, Data Engineering, Business Intelligence and Data Product Management.

We'd love to hear from you if you have...🔍

Experience using analytics to support business decisions, answer complex commercial questions and identify opportunities for improvement.Strong SQL skills and confidence working with large datasets to produce accurate, reliable and well-structured analysis.The ability to structure analytical work clearly, navigate ambiguity and turn complex findings into actionable recommendations.Experience communicating insight to a range of audiences, including senior stakeholders and colleagues from technical and non-technical backgrounds.Strong data visualisation skills, ideally using tools such as Tableau, Power BI or similar.A thoughtful approach to storytelling, with the ability to create polished deliverables that make insight easy to understand and act on.Strong organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple analytical work streams and balance competing priorities.Ideally, experience with DBT or modern data transformation workflows, and exposure to analysing experiments, pilots or trials.

More Information

Enjoy fantastic perks like private healthcare & dental insurance, a generous work from abroad policy, 2-for-1 share purchase plans, an EV Scheme to further reduce carbon emissions, extra festive time off, and excellent family-friendly benefits.

We prioritise career growth with clear career paths, transparent pay bands, personal learning budgets, and regular learning days. Jump on board and supercharge your career from day one!

We're operating a hybrid model and ask that Trainliners work from the office a minimum of 60% of their time over a 12-week period. We also have a 28-day Work from Abroad policy.

Our Values Represent The Things That Matter Most To Us And What We Live And Breathe Everyday, In Everything We Do

💭 Think Big - We're building the future of rail ✔️ Own It - We focus on every customer, partner and journey 🤝 Travel Together - We're one team ♻️ Do Good - We make a positive impact 

We know that having a diverse team makes us better and helps us succeed. And we mean all forms of diversity - gender, ethnicity, sexuality, disability, nationality and diversity of thought. That's why we're committed to creating inclusive places to work, where everyone belongs and differences are valued and celebrated.

Interested in finding out more about what it's like to work at Trainline? Why not check us out on LinkedIn, Instagram and Glassdoor!

rows.title: Data Analyst - Participant Support Operations & Clinical Operations
rows.descriptionText:
We have an exciting opportunity for a Data Analyst to join our Analytics team, using data and operational insight to help improve both the participant experience and the journey of biosamples through our study.You'll work closely with operational and technical teams to understand performance, investigate complex problems and turn data into practical recommendations. From understanding participant contact volumes and service demand to identifying bottlenecks across biosample logistics, your analysis will help teams make better decisions, improve processes and deliver more efficient and reliable operations.Despite big improvements in healthcare in our lifetimes, today millions of people in the UK still live in poor health as they get older. Diseases like cancer, dementia, diabetes, and heart disease affect the lives of many people in our communities. Our goal is to create a world-leading resource for health research, to improve our understanding and spot the patterns of how and why common diseases start, so treatments can begin sooner and be more effective.Our Future Health will be the UK's largest ever health research programme, bringing people together to develop new ways to detect, prevent, and treat diseases. We are a charity, supported by the UK Government, in partnership with charities and industry. We work closely with the NHS and with public authorities across all nations and regions of the UK.What you'll be doing:In this role, you'll partner with teams across Participant Support Operations, Clinical Operations and Analytics to solve operational problems using data and evidence. You'll develop trusted reporting and metrics, investigate issues across multiple systems and help teams move towards more proactive, data-informed performance management.Your key responsibilities will include but not be limited to:Analyse participant contact volumes, service performance, complaints and backlogs, using forecasting and capacity planning to help teams understand and manage demandIdentify trends and drivers within participant enquiries and complaints, turning your findings into actionable recommendations to improve participant experience and operational efficiencyAnalyse the end-to-end biosample journey across operational, logistics and laboratory systems, identifying delays, discrepancies, anomalies and quality issuesUse SQL and exploratory analysis to investigate data across multiple systems, reconstruct operational workflows and identify the root causes of issuesDevelop and maintain operational reporting, performance metrics and monitoring across participant support and biosample operationsWork with Analytics Engineers, Data Scientists and operational teams to improve data quality, traceability and reporting capabilityTranslate operational questions into structured analytical approaches and communicate findings clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholdersHelp teams move from manual and reactive reporting towards proactive performance management and data-informed decision-makingYou'll be part of a wider Analytics function made up of analysts, data scientists and data engineers. The team works remotely, coming together in person twice a month for collaboration and co-working, as well as quarterly strategy days focused on planning, problem-solving and longer-term thinking. We also have a regular book club and team demos, which give us space to learn together and celebrate what we're building. 
Hiring Process We feel hiring should be transparent and give you a real sense for what Our Future Health is like. Here's what you can expect: Initial chat with our Talent team (30 min) to get to know each other, discuss the role, and answer any questions you have1st interview with our Analytics Manager (25 min) - this is an opportunity to meet your potential line manager and for you both to align on role expectationsTechnical interview with 2-3 members from our Analytics team (60 min). This will include a short task you'll need to prepare in advance of the interview and is designed to get a sense for how you'd approach the real-world responsibilities of this roleFinal stage competency interview (60 min) with a small cross-functional panel of your potential new stakeholders. This will focus on how you collaborate, work with stakeholders, and navigate ambiguity and challenges in real-world projects

Requirements

We recognise that candidates may have developed relevant experience through different career paths and welcome applications from those who can demonstrate many, though not necessarily all, of the skills and experience listed below:Strong SQL skills and experience working with relational databases and cloud data platforms such as SnowflakeExperience analysing complex operational data from multiple systems and investigating data quality issues, discrepancies and operational risksExperience developing and maintaining reporting, dashboards, datasets or other analytical products used by operational teamsAn understanding of operational performance analysis, which could have been developed within areas such as healthcare, logistics, customer operations, participant services, research or another complex operational environmentFamiliarity with data modelling concepts and experience collaborating with Analytics Engineering or Data Engineering teamsStrong problem-solving skills, with the ability to investigate root causes and turn analysis into practical recommendationsThe ability to communicate complex analytical findings clearly and build effective relationships with both operational and technical stakeholdersAn organised and adaptable approach, with the ability to manage competing priorities while maintaining a high level of accuracy and attention to data qualityKnowledge of forecasting, capacity planning, performance measurement or operational analytics methodologies would be advantageousAn understanding of statistical concepts and performance monitoring techniques, such as variation analysis or statistical process control, would be beneficialExperience using Python or R for data manipulation, analysis, automation or exploratory investigation would also be beneficial. 

Benefits

From £53,000 annum basic salary.Generous Pension Scheme - We invest in your future with employer contributions of up to 12%30 Days Holiday + Bank Holidays - Enjoy a generous holiday allowance with the flexibility to take bank holidays when it suits youEnhanced Parental Leave - Supporting you during life's biggest momentsCycle to Work Scheme - Save 25-39% on a new bike and accessories through salary sacrificeHome & Tech Savings - Get up to 8% off on IKEA and Currys products, spreading the cost over 12 months through salary sacrifice£1,000 Employee Referral Bonus - Know someone amazing? Get rewarded for bringing them on board!Wellbeing Support - Access to Mental Health First Aiders, plus 24/7 online GP services and an Employee Assistance Programme for you and your familyA Great Place to Work - We have a lovely Central London office in Holborn, and offer flexible and remote working arrangementsJoin us - let's prevent disease together.Closing date: 12 October 2026 at 5:00 pmWe may close this vacancy earlier than the advertised closing date if we receive a high volume of applications, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.At Our Future Health, we recognise the importance of having a diverse workforce and ensuring that all candidates, regardless of their background, have equitable access to our application process. We proactively encourage applicants who identify as having a disability, neurodiversity, or long-term health conditions to let us know if they require any reasonable adjustments as part of their application process.If you do require any reasonable adjustments, please email us at talent@ourfuturehealth.org.uk.
