Position: Federal Data Analyst

Location: Boston

About Pryzm

Pryzm is transforming how companies engage with the federal government. Today, federal procurement and BD is fragmented across disconnected workflows, siloed intelligence, and institutional knowledge locked in spreadsheets and inboxes. Pryzm brings together market intelligence, budget data, program visibility, and human insights into a single platform that helps teams navigate and win in the federal ecosystem. Pryzm is backed by Tier 1 investors including a16z, and is trusted by organizations across the national security and federal technology ecosystem. Our mission is simple: deliver the best capabilities to the missions that matter most.

The Role

Pryzm's platform depends on data that most companies don't even attempt to track well. We're looking for a Federal Data Analyst to help own that data, keeping it accurate, useful, and ahead of what our customers need. The role blends technical data work with market-facing analysis, and touches everything from day-to-day data quality to the insights we put in front of customers.

rows.title: Intermediate Applied Operations Research Analyst
rows.descriptionText:
At MITRE, your passion fuels work that impacts our nation and improves lives. This is where your skills strengthen national security, cybersecurity, health, transportation, and citizen services. We’re a nonprofit engineering, applied research, and advanced technology organization working in the public interest. With objectivity and integrity at our core, we lead federally funded research and development centers for U.S. government agencies – collaborating with industry and academia to deliver integrated, high-impact solutions that advance our nation’s health, security, and prosperity. Our people tackle the toughest technical challenges, supported by competitive benefits, meaningful career development, and a culture of innovation, collaboration, and technical excellence. Choose MITRE for a career with purpose — and help shape the future.

Department Summary:

This is an opportunity for a motivated Operations Research Analyst to join MITRE’s Operations Analysis department. We are a large group of over 60 operations research professionals, including over 20 PhDs, who provide thought leadership on a variety of strategic and technical issues, perform analysis that enable our sponsors to make more effective decisions, lead internal research and development activities to bring new technical capabilities into the public sector, and serve as trusted third-party advisors to government sponsors on a variety of technical topics.

In short, we apply our problem-solving skills to complex interdisciplinary problems that occur within or at the intersection of organizations, operations, and technology. We support sponsor projects across the defense and public sectors including homeland defense, military logistics, radio-spectrum frequency management, health care delivery, cybersecurity analytics, fraud detection, satellite planning, homeland security and civilian aviation. We apply advanced analytic techniques such as longitudinal analysis, large-scale integer programming, metaheuristics, agent-based modeling, reinforcement learning, predictive modeling, mathematical modeling, time series & forecasting, machine learning, optimization, statistics, probability modeling, regression analyses, Bayesian analysis, and different types of simulation to solve the nation’s toughest problems. And our research pushes the boundaries on topics such as complex scheduling, medical image analysis, identifying changes in data streams and incorporating the latest AI advancements into our processes for efficiency and rigor.

If you are passionate about project-based analytical work in the public interest, you have found the right place.

Roles & Responsibilities:

Apply advanced analytical and mathematical modeling techniques to inform difficult policy and acquisition decisions, to maximize operational effectiveness and efficiency, and achieve highest quality engineering solutionsFrame problems, collect and manipulate data, develop & code customized algorithms, identify risks, and incorporate domain-specific context, as necessary & applicable, to supplement and enhance insight gained solely from mathematical analysesPresent results in an intuitive, actionable manner that can be understood by all sponsor audiences, regardless of technical expertise, including creative data visualization artifactsWork independently and collaborate with a team of technical staff and domain expertsWork successfully both in a remote environment and with in-person presence

Basic Qualifications:

Typically requires a minimum of 2 years of related experience with a Bachelor’s degree in Operations Research, Industrial Engineering, Data Science/Analytics, Applied Mathematics/Statistics, or equivalent knowledge and skills in a related field or an advanced degree with relevant experience who can immediately contribute at this job step; or equivalent combination of related education and work experience.Be passionate about applying operations research, statistics, and data analytics to real world problemsBe willing to adapt and learnDemonstrated ability to use at least one optimization package (e.g., Gurobi, CPLEX, PuLP, AMPL)Demonstrated ability to use at least one modern programming language (e.g., Python, R, Java)Demonstrated ability to use at least one simulation platform (e.g., Stella, Simio, Arena, AnyLogic, SimPy, RSimmer)Must have an active Secret U.S Government issued Security Clearance and must be eligible to obtain and maintain a Top Secret U.S Government issued Security Clearance. Per the U.S. Government’s eligibility requirements, you must be a U.S Citizen to be considered for a security clearance.This position requires 4 days a week on site

Preferred Qualifications:

Master’s degree in Operations Research, Industrial Engineering, Data Science/Analytics, Applied Mathematics/Statistics, or equivalent knowledge and skills in a related fieldPreference given to qualified candidates with active clearance (e.g. TS/SCI)Experience working with/for agencies and/or departments of the US Government (e.g., FAA, DoD, DoE, DHS, Treasury, IRS)Demonstrated ability to develop and incorporate a variety of AI/ML models, techniques, and principles into analytical work to efficiently achieve rigorous outcomesFamiliarity and/or experience with Electromagnetic Spectrum (EMS) organizations, concepts, modeling, testing, and assessment, to include the Joint Electromagnetic Spectrum Operations Center (JEC), Joint Electromagnetic Warfare Center (JEWC), Electromagnetic Spectrum Operations (EMSO), Electromagnetic Battle Management—Joint (EMBM-J), Spectrum Consumption Modeling (SCM), and Electronic Warfare (EW)Familiarity and/or experience with the Mission Engineering paradigm of decomposing a key operational problem, establishing a system-of-systems model of components, technology, policies, procedures, and techniques, and ultimately simulating the process on a technical platform

This requisition requires the candidate to have a minimum of the following clearance(s):

Secret

This requisition requires the hired candidate to have or obtain, within one year from the date of hire, the following clearance(s):

Top Secret

$98,800 - $123,500 - $148,200 Annual

Onsite

We enable clients to seize new opportunities, improve performance, and increase shareholder value within complex and converging industries.

Trusted Leader with Industry Expertise and Innovative Approaches 

As the leading pure play communications and media strategy consulting group globally, we assist operating companies and financial groups in fast, high-impact, confident decision making Deep industry knowledge and advanced analytics allow us to develop more actionable insights and recommendations, delivering better advice, more quickly – we succeed in building long-term client relationships because of the results we deliver Altman Solon's industry focus and shorter average project duration allow employees to quickly gain exposure to a breadth of projects and develop an expertise in TMT along with a sophisticated consulting toolkit

rows.title: Research Analyst, Community Insights
rows.descriptionText:
THE ROLE: Research Analyst, Community Insights

Britebound is a national non-profit with a mission to support middle and high school learners to explore their interests, experience potential careers, and navigate a path to a meaningful and rewarding future. We fulfill our mission through free digital-first experiences, grantmaking, policy advocacy, research, and impact investing.

We believe that exploring career possibilities, as early as middle school, and providing access to education-to-career pathways aligned with one’s passions and goals will result in greater confidence and long-term success for all students.

We are looking for a Research Analyst, Community Insights. This role will partner closely with the Research & Insights team and colleagues across Britebound on internal- and external-facing research, while owning the strategy and day-to-day effectiveness of our online research communities.

What You’ll Do 

Research & Data Analysis: Ensure data integrity through data cleaning, validation, and preparation across diverse datasets; produce topline statistics, subgroup comparisons, and multivariate analyses that address key research questions.Apply statistical methods such as regression analysis, clustering, significance testing, and driver analysis to uncover insights, explain variation in outcomes, and identify actionable findings.Translate complex findings into clear charts, captions, visualizations, dashboards, reports, briefs, and presentations that are compelling and accessible to non-technical audiences.Online Research Community Management : Manage Britebound’s three distinct online research communities (teens, parents, and counselors).Engage with internal Britebound teams to design and conduct weekly research engagements to meet team needs. Synthesize and deliver findings on a quick-turnaround cadence.Design and program research engagements based on organizational needs for teen, parent, and counselor online communities.Lead the launch and ongoing management of Britebound’s new counselor community, including recruitment, engagement, research programming, and continuous improvement of the member experience.Online Community Strategy: Develop and steward Britebound’s overarching strategy for online research communities, establishing consistent approaches to recruitment, retention, incentives, engagement, research cadence, governance, and insight sharing across audiences.Collaboration & Leadership: Help shape the Research & Insights team’s research agenda and analytical approaches; build strong cross-functional relationships to identify shared research needs and advance data-driven initiatives across Britebound.Contribute to Research & Insights reports by activating Britebound’s online communities to source relevant qualitative feedback that adds depth and context to quantitative findings.Propose and develop strategies for creating dashboards or other data visualizations that enable impactful use of findings from online research communities and other Britebound research projects.
About You

5-10 years of experience in research, polling, analytics, community-based research, or a related role, with a proven track record of completing complex analyses, working with rich datasets, and developing clear data visualizations.Strong quantitative and analytical skills, including experience with tools such as R, SQL, Python, STATA, SPSS, Dataiku, and/or comparable platforms; able to synthesize complex information and develop actionable insights.Experience building, managing, or engaging online communities, panels, or research participant networks; skilled in recruitment, retention, incentive strategy, moderation, and translating member feedback into usable insights.Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to turn quantitative and qualitative findings into concise, audience-appropriate stories and recommendations.Able to connect the big picture to execution, manage multiple workstreams and deadlines, and proactively identify opportunities to improve research quality and business impact.Collaborative, adaptable, resilient, results-oriented, and comfortable engaging in constructive debate and incorporating diverse perspectives. rows.title: Senior AI Engineer I
rows.descriptionText:
About The Role

As a Senior AI Engineer I embedded within Secure Power, you leverage generative AI, automation platforms, and low-code tooling to solve real operational problems and remove manual work from the team’s day-to-day. You build, test, and deploy AI agents, automated workflows, and dashboards while maintaining the integrations and infrastructure that keep them running. Your core responsibilities include translating business rules and decision logic into reliable agent instructions, converting manual processes into automated workflows, and building the dashboards leadership relies on to track performance. You automate processes for Secure Power to enhance efficiency and collaborate with process owners and team leaders to develop working prototypes and production-ready tools.

Your mission is to apply specialized technical expertise in AI and automation to identify inefficiencies, map processes, and build new tools that address Secure Power’s most persistent operational pain points. Your work directly impacts how Secure Power runs day to day – contributing to faster cycle times, cleaner data, and better visibility for leadership. You are a specialized technical expert in AI engineering, focused on the delivery, implementation, and design of AI agents, automation, and reporting tools embedded within a single business team. You apply broad technical knowledge to deliver results with direct, visible impact on Secure Power’s operations. You make decisions regarding your own work and priorities, often guided by established precedents, technical standards, and some interpretation. You are responsible for guiding other professionals and providing mentorship on non-routine or escalated issues, and your work is reviewed for accuracy and quality to ensure the highest standards of AI engineering are met.

What You Will Do

Build and deploy AI agents (e.g., using Microsoft Copilot Studio) that solve real Secure Power business problems Design and maintain the automation and dashboard infrastructure (Power Automate, Power Apps, Power BI, Smartsheet) that supports scalable, production-grade solutions for the team. Collaborate with process owners and team leaders to map current-state workflows, redesign broken or redundant steps, and transform them into working prototypes and Minimum Viable Products (MVPs). Automate workflows and processes across systems the team already uses – including Salesforce, Oracle, CPQ, and SharePoint – to boost efficiency and remove manual re-entry. Run pilots, gather feedback, and iterate quickly; create simple documentation so the team can use and own what you’ve built. Collaborate with the central AI team and ensure all AI solutions adhere to established governance, security, and responsible AI policies. 

Required Skills

AI Agent Development: Building, training, and deploying AI agents (e.g., Copilot Studio) into real production use. Workflow Automation: Implementing and deploying automated workflows in low-code platforms (e.g., Power Automate, Power Apps). Process Mapping & Redesign: Mapping current-state workflows end-to-end and identifying where automation will – and won’t – add value. Data Integration: Connecting AI and automation tools across enterprise systems via API (e.g., Salesforce, Oracle) to eliminate manual data re-entry. Prompt & Logic Design: Translating business rules and decision logic into clear, testable agent instructions. Responsible AI & Governance: Applying data privacy, security, and responsible AI practices, including human review where outputs affect a customer or an order. 

Qualifications For Success

Strong problem-solving mindset with the ability to handle ambiguous, undocumented processes independently. Excellent collaboration skills with cross-functional teams to translate business requirements into technical solutions. Growth-oriented mindset with strong curiosity to explore new AI and automation technologies and methodologies. Adaptability to changing priorities and the ability to navigate a fast-moving, embedded team environment with ease. Comfortable explaining a technical tradeoff to a non-technical stakeholder or leader. 

Benefits & Growth

Work on AI and automation projects that directly impact how an entire business team operates. Collaborate with Secure Power leaders, process owners, and the central AI team in a supportive, innovation-driven culture. Access continuous learning opportunities, certifications, and technical mentorship

At Schneider, we believe that every employee is a talent who deserves equal opportunities. This means you matter. Every individual needs to feel valued, supported, and treated fairly to do their best work.

Our Total Rewards is our way of saying: “We see you. We value you”. It’s more than just pay and benefits- it’s a meaningful investment in you. It is designed for you to perform, grow, feel safe, and elevate your potential to shine as an impact maker.

For this U.S. based position, the expected pay range is USD 101,600 - USD 152,400 per year. This pay range includes base pay and short-term incentives. The compensation range for this full-time position applies to candidates located within the United States. Our pay ranges are determined by reviewing roles of similar responsibility and level. Within the pay range, individual pay is determined by several factors including performance, knowledge, job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

Schneider Electric is there when it matters most to you

We are growing our Applied AI org and seeking Machine Learning Engineers with expertise in model training, evaluation, and production-oriented ML systems. Experience building, training, adapting, or evaluating machine learning models.Strong software engineering skills in Python and modern ML frameworks such as PyTorch, JAX, or TensorFlow.Experience designing experiments, evaluation metrics, or test sets for model performance.Ability to debug model behavior using data, traces, logs, and qualitative feedback.Experience working across research and engineering teams to move ML capabilities into usable systems.Familiarity with large language models, multi-modal models, or agentic AI systems.Clear communication skills for translating customer needs into technical model improvements.

About Ironwood

Ironwood Pharmaceuticals (Nasdaq: IRWD), is a biotechnology company focused on developing and commercializing therapies for people living with gastrointestinal (GI) and rare diseases. Ironwood is advancing apraglutide, a next-generation, long-acting synthetic GLP-2 analog being developed for patients with short bowel syndrome who are dependent on parenteral support. Ironwood has also been a pioneer in the development of LINZESS® (linaclotide), the U.S. branded prescription market leader for adults with irritable bowel syndrome with constipation (IBS-C) or chronic idiopathic constipation (CIC) and pediatric patients with IBS-C or functional constipation (FC).

Founded in 1998, Ironwood is headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts, with additional operations in Basel, Switzerland.

rows.title: Intellia Therapeutics – Global Health Economics and Outcomes Research Postdoctoral Research Fellow
rows.descriptionText:
About The Opportunity

About the Opportunity

Northeastern University Pharmaceutical Industry Fellowships Program is a two-year experiential program designed to advance lifelong learning and the education and training of Pharm.D. graduates. A key element of the program’s success is preparing Fellows to meet evolving workforce needs across various sectors of the pharmaceutical industry.

Fellows have the opportunity to work closely with our innovative biopharmaceutical industry partners, while engaging with Northeastern University faculty in professional and career development, teaching, service, and scholarly activities.

In partnership with Northeastern University, Intellia Therapeutics is offering a two-year Health economics and outcomes research (HEOR) fellowship, based in Cambridge, MA.

About Intellia

Intellia Therapeutics is a Cambridge-based biotechnology company focused on developing clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR)-based gene editing therapies to transform lives of people with severe diseases. In fact, Intellia’s co-founder Jennifer Doudna along with Emmanuelle Charpentier were awarded the 2020 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for their pioneering work in CRISPR.

At Intellia, we are humbled to contribute to what we believe to be medical history. As a leader in this field, our responsibility and commitment to patients is critical in our pursuit of developing novel, potentially curative therapeutics utilizing CRISPR-based technologies.

More specifically, we are employing a modular gene editing platform to create diverse in vivo and ex vivo therapeutics, spanning a range of disease indications. Guided by this full-spectrum approach, we are committed to making CRISPR-based medicines a reality for people living with genetic diseases and to creating novel engineered cell therapies for various cancers and autoimmune diseases.

Intellia HEOR Fellowship Program Overview

Northeastern University Pharmaceutical Industry Fellowships Program is a 2-year experiential program designed to advance lifelong learning and the education and training of PharmD/MPH/PhD graduates. A key element of the program’s success is preparing Fellows to meet evolving workforce needs across various sectors of the pharmaceutical industry. Fellows have the opportunity to work closely with our innovative biopharmaceutical industry partners, while engaging with Northeastern University faculty in professional and career development, teaching, service, and scholarly activities. In partnership with Northeastern University, Intellia Therapeutics is offering a 2-year Global HEOR and Evidence Strategy fellowship, based in Cambridge, MA.

What Sets the Intellia Fellowship Apart?

During the program, Fellows will work collaboratively and cross-functionally in Intellia’s HEOR and Evidence Strategy team, gaining exposure to our high-energy, fast-paced, and supportive culture. The HEOR and Evidence Strategy team sits within the Market Access and Patient Services team in the Commercial Organization. At Intellia, a technical and scientific expertise background is highly valued. The Fellowship offers a uniquely structured experience, beginning with a foundational year working with the Director, HEOR and Evidence Strategy supporting the HEOR strategy for Intellia’s novel, gene-editing therapies. This foundational year provides the Fellow with a strong understanding of strategic development of value and evidence generation strategy to support clinical development and commercial brand plans. In the second year, the Fellow will have an option to participate in 1-3 projects / activities within the broader Market Access and Patient Services team. These optional activities will aim to give the Fellow exposure to key strategic or execution activities that fall within Field HEOR and Market Access Strategy. This will allow the Fellow to gain blended exposure across Intellia’s dynamic business functions and build a versatile skill set for a future in biotech.

Responsibilities

rows.title: ML Engineer, Applied AI
rows.descriptionText:
Your Impact at LILA

We are growing our Applied AI org and seeking Machine Learning Engineers with expertise in model training, evaluation, and production-oriented ML systems. You’ll work on improving Lila’s AI models for customer-specific scientific needs, with a focus on turning frontier model capabilities into reliable workflows that can be evaluated, iterated, and used in real customer contexts. This is a rare chance to join an early team with the autonomy, flexibility, and compute to tackle frontier science problems.

Applied AI sits at the intersection of AI Research, model engineering, and product deployment. The team partners closely with AI Researchers and Software teams to adapt Lila models to customer workflows, improve model quality through experimentation, and ensure model behavior works well end to end inside the application.

This role is ideal for someone who can bridge research and engineering: training or adapting models, building evaluation loops, debugging model behavior, and collaborating across AI and Software to move promising capabilities into production-quality systems.

What You'll Be Building

Close the last-mile gap between Lila AI model capabilities and customer-specific scientific workflows.Post-train models using approaches such as SFT and RL (DPO, PPO/GRPO) to align model behavior with customer-specific requirements and feedback.Build evaluation loops that measure model quality, reliability, and customer fit.Design experiments to improve model performance across applied customer use cases.Feed customer learnings, data signals, and evaluation results back into the Lila AI model improvement cycles.Partner with AI researchers to translate model improvements into usable capabilities.Work with Software to integrate model behavior into end-to-end product workflows.Debug model failures using traces, evaluations, customer context, and scientific feedback.Build reusable tooling for model adaptation, evaluation, and deployment workflows.

What You'll Need To Succeed

Experience building, training, adapting, or evaluating machine learning models.Strong software engineering skills in Python and modern ML frameworks such as PyTorch, JAX, or TensorFlow.Experience designing experiments, evaluation metrics, or test sets for model performance.Ability to debug model behavior using data, traces, logs, and qualitative feedback.Experience working across research and engineering teams to move ML capabilities into usable systems.Familiarity with large language models, multi-modal models, or agentic AI systems.Clear communication skills for translating customer needs into technical model improvements.

Bonus Points For

Experience adapting models for customer-facing or production workflows.Experience with scientific, technical, or data-intensive customer use cases.Experience building evaluation harnesses, model monitoring, or quality dashboards.Familiarity with retrieval-augmented generation, tool use, or agentic workflows.Experience with RL post-training, such as RLHF, GRPO, or tool-augmented RL.Experience training MoE architectures.Experience working with product or customer-facing teams to translate needs into ML improvements.

Lila Sciences is building Scientific Superintelligence™ to solve humankind's greatest challenges. We believe science is the most inspiring frontier for AI. Rather than hard-coding expert knowledge into tools, LILA builds systems that can learn for themselves.

rows.title: Senior AI Engineer I
rows.descriptionText:
About The Role

As a Senior AI Engineer I embedded within Secure Power, you leverage generative AI, automation platforms, and low-code tooling to solve real operational problems and remove manual work from the team’s day-to-day. You build, test, and deploy AI agents, automated workflows, and dashboards while maintaining the integrations and infrastructure that keep them running. Your core responsibilities include translating business rules and decision logic into reliable agent instructions, converting manual processes into automated workflows, and building the dashboards leadership relies on to track performance. You automate processes for Secure Power to enhance efficiency and collaborate with process owners and team leaders to develop working prototypes and production-ready tools.

Your mission is to apply specialized technical expertise in AI and automation to identify inefficiencies, map processes, and build new tools that address Secure Power’s most persistent operational pain points. Your work directly impacts how Secure Power runs day to day – contributing to faster cycle times, cleaner data, and better visibility for leadership. You are a specialized technical expert in AI engineering, focused on the delivery, implementation, and design of AI agents, automation, and reporting tools embedded within a single business team. You apply broad technical knowledge to deliver results with direct, visible impact on Secure Power’s operations. You make decisions regarding your own work and priorities, often guided by established precedents, technical standards, and some interpretation. You are responsible for guiding other professionals and providing mentorship on non-routine or escalated issues, and your work is reviewed for accuracy and quality to ensure the highest standards of AI engineering are met.

What You Will Do

Build and deploy AI agents (e.g., using Microsoft Copilot Studio) that solve real Secure Power business problems Design and maintain the automation and dashboard infrastructure (Power Automate, Power Apps, Power BI, Smartsheet) that supports scalable, production-grade solutions for the team. Collaborate with process owners and team leaders to map current-state workflows, redesign broken or redundant steps, and transform them into working prototypes and Minimum Viable Products (MVPs). Automate workflows and processes across systems the team already uses – including Salesforce, Oracle, CPQ, and SharePoint – to boost efficiency and remove manual re-entry. Run pilots, gather feedback, and iterate quickly; create simple documentation so the team can use and own what you’ve built. Collaborate with the central AI team and ensure all AI solutions adhere to established governance, security, and responsible AI policies. 

Required Skills

AI Agent Development: Building, training, and deploying AI agents (e.g., Copilot Studio) into real production use. Workflow Automation: Implementing and deploying automated workflows in low-code platforms (e.g., Power Automate, Power Apps). Process Mapping & Redesign: Mapping current-state workflows end-to-end and identifying where automation will – and won’t – add value. Data Integration: Connecting AI and automation tools across enterprise systems via API (e.g., Salesforce, Oracle) to eliminate manual data re-entry. Prompt & Logic Design: Translating business rules and decision logic into clear, testable agent instructions. Responsible AI & Governance: Applying data privacy, security, and responsible AI practices, including human review where outputs affect a customer or an order. 

Qualifications For Success

Strong problem-solving mindset with the ability to handle ambiguous, undocumented processes independently. Excellent collaboration skills with cross-functional teams to translate business requirements into technical solutions. Growth-oriented mindset with strong curiosity to explore new AI and automation technologies and methodologies. Adaptability to changing priorities and the ability to navigate a fast-moving, embedded team environment with ease. Comfortable explaining a technical tradeoff to a non-technical stakeholder or leader. 

Benefits & Growth

Collaborate with Secure Power leaders, process owners, and the central AI team in a supportive, innovation-driven culture. Access continuous learning opportunities, certifications, and technical mentorship

rows.descriptionText:
About The Opportunity

About the Opportunity

Northeastern University Pharmaceutical Industry Fellowships Program is a two-year experiential program designed to advance lifelong learning and the education and training of Pharm.D. graduates. A key element of the program’s success is preparing Fellows to meet evolving workforce needs across various sectors of the pharmaceutical industry.

Fellows have the opportunity to work closely with our innovative biopharmaceutical industry partners, while engaging with Northeastern University faculty in professional and career development, teaching, service, and scholarly activities.

In partnership with Northeastern University, Vertex Pharmaceuticals Incorporated (Vertex) is offering a two-year Global Regulatory Affairs (GRA) fellowship, based in Boston, MA.

About Vertex

Vertex is a global biotechnology company that invests in scientific innovation to create transformative medicines for people with serious diseases and conditions. The company has approved therapies for cystic fibrosis, sickle cell disease, transfusion-dependent beta thalassemia and acute pain, and it continues to advance clinical and research programs in these areas. Vertex also has a robust clinical pipeline of investigational therapies across a range of modalities in other serious diseases where it has deep insight into causal human biology, including IgA nephropathy, neuropathic pain, APOL1-mediated kidney disease, primary membranous nephropathy, autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease, type 1 diabetes, generalized myasthenia gravis, and myotonic dystrophy type 1.

Vertex was founded in 1989 and has its global headquarters in Boston, with international headquarters in London. Additionally, the company has research and development sites and commercial offices in North America, Europe, Australia, Latin America and the Middle East. Vertex is consistently recognized as one of the industry's top places to work, including 16 consecutive years on Science magazine's Top Employers list and one of Fortune’s 100 Best Companies to Work For. For company updates and to learn more about Vertex's history of innovation, visit www.vrtx.com or follow us on LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram, YouTube and X.

Responsibilities

The PharmD fellow(s) will have an opportunity to gain specialized and in-depth training in two distinct areas of GRA, Regulatory Strategy and Global Labeling, for a period of 8 months each. The remaining 8 months of the program will be spent in a regulatory elective. Regulatory elective opportunities are offered in areas including CMC, Advertising and Promotion, International, Policy, and Strategic Operations. Specific opportunities may vary depending on the interests of the PharmD fellow(s) as well as the needs of the department. Overall, the structured program will provide a cumulative set of skills that will help facilitate a smooth transition to a successful career after the fellowship.

Global Labeling

Provide strategic guidance on labeling regulations, competitor labeling, and labeling trendsLead team in negotiating and maintaining competitive labeling with health authorities globally


Regulatory Strategy

Job Description

Job Summary:

We are seeking a highly motivated Automation Scientist to join the Data, AI & Genome Sciences team at our Company Research Laboratories in Cambridge, MA. In this role, you will operate, maintain, and optimize advanced automation platforms and laboratory instrumentation to support drug discovery and development programs. The successful candidate will manage multiple projects, develop and improve automated workflows, analyze experimental results, troubleshoot system issues, and ensure reliable operation of automated systems. Experience with automated liquid handlers, laboratory robotics, and analytical instruments is required, along with strong attention to detail, problem-solving skills, and the ability to follow and validate scientific protocols in a fast-paced, innovative environment.

Responsibilities

Collaborate closely with experimental biologists, data analysts, and therapeutic area subject matter experts to develop and implement scalable automation workflows that enable high-quality, reproducible data generation in a timely manner. Design and execute large-scale automation protocols for cutting-edge single-cell and molecular assays (e.g., Parse-seq, 10x Flex, CROP-seq/Perturb-seq, Olink HT, immune profiling, Multiome ATAC-seq), high-throughput CRISPR screens, and complex 3D model generation using a variety of liquid handlers and robotic instruments. Proactively engage with cross-functional teams across Genome Sciences, Discovery & Analytical Genomics Sciences (DAGS), Therapeutic Areas (TAs), and IT to drive impact on early drug discovery efforts under accelerated timelines. Clearly communicate objectives, assay protocols, and experimental results through detailed presentations and reports to stakeholders and senior leadership.

Master’s degree in engineering or life sciences Bachelor’s degree in engineering or life science with a minimum of 3 years of hands-on experience in laboratory automation within academia, pharmaceutical, or biotechnology settings.

Extensive hands-on experience in laboratory automation for molecular biology applications, with a strong focus on high-throughput genomic technologies such as single-cell RNA-seq, Olink HT, CRISPR-based screens, and 3D cell culture models. About The Opportunity

About the Opportunity

Northeastern University Pharmaceutical Industry Fellowships Program is a two-year experiential program designed to advance lifelong learning and the education and training of Pharm.D. graduates. A key element of the program’s success is preparing Fellows to meet evolving workforce needs across various sectors of the pharmaceutical industry.

Fellows have the opportunity to work closely with our innovative biopharmaceutical industry partners, while engaging with Northeastern University faculty in professional and career development, teaching, service, and scholarly activities.

In partnership with Northeastern University, CSL Seqirus is offering a two-year Medical Affairs fellowship, based in Waltham, Massachusetts.

About CSL Seqirus

At CSL Seqirus, we are driven by just one goal - to lessen the severity and impact of influenza, which can reach epidemic or even pandemic proportions with life-threatening consequences. Every year our influenza vaccines help protect millions of people. We find solutions to big, complex, challenging problems, and we see the results in the world around us. Then we do it all over again the following year.

CSL Seqirus is one of the world’s largest influenza vaccine companies. We were created when our parent company, CSL Limited, acquired the Novartis influenza vaccine business and combined its vaccine subsidiary, bioCSL.

The Medical Affairs fellow will assist across all pertinent areas of medical affairs within CSL Seqirus. The fellow will have rotations in medical information, publications, scientific communications, field-based US medical science liaison and will also have the opportunity to specialize in a preferred area of medical affairs for an elective rotation. The fellow will help the team to develop the strategy and implementation surrounding the collection, preparation, and dissemination of medical and scientific information on CSL Seqirus’ products externally to health care providers, health care institutions, patients and their families, and internally to CSL Seqirus partners in multiple countries.

The fellow’s portfolio will span all CSL Seqirus pipeline and marketed products in the region.

Responsibilities

 Develops and maintains a broad knowledge of medical, scientific, and technical information for therapeutic area and product portfolio, becoming a scientific influenza expert for Medical Information. Assist with creation and reviews of key medical communication documents, including, but not limited to, Scientific Responses Documents (SRDs), Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs), content for medical meetings/symposia/Advisory Boards, content for internal Medical Affairs staff training and Data-on-File. Ensures prompt and accurate, quality-assured documents are created in alignment with the Global and Regional Medical Affairs scientific messages and strategy. Creates and implements processes/procedures for a streamlined handling of medical inquiries. Partners cross functionally to ensure data is incorporated into content and process is in place for highest volume topics for customers. Assist with the Publications, Abstracts and Posters; helps to facilitate Team calls to review progress of manuscripts and congress planning progress. Arrange for medical writing support once publication plan is recognized. Ensure that the vendor selected is trained on internal policies, Good Publication Practice (GPP) Guidelines, internal compliance requirements and authorship criteria. Ensure consistent cross-functional communication and collaboration on ongoing publication projects and project updates with key stakeholders internally and externally. Assist with updating important internal documents such as the Scientific Pillars and Platforms and product compendia to support the Medical Plan and Medical Communication strategy. Assist with the oversight of manuscript submission for RD disclosure review including manuscripts (primary and secondary), abstracts and posters for review and approval prior to submission to journals and congresses. Assist with medical content review for professional materials through the Promotional Review Committee (PRC). Works with the medical affairs team to evaluate and review promotional materials. Seeks to build and maintain collaborative relationships with all involved in the PRC process and sets a model for professional and productive interactions. Ensures timely medical support for Promotional Review Committee (medical review of promotional materials) is accomplished for all CSL Seqirus’ products. Ensure that strategically aligned scientific communication is medically accurate and supported by appropriate data. Participate in the development of unbranded and branded commercial programs ensuring that they are medically accurate. Provide medical input and advice into development of commercial campaigns, where applicable and ensure that timely support and accuracy for Promotional Review Committee is accomplished for all CSL Seqirus’ vaccines, in the United States. Assist with Identifying appropriate regional Key Opinion Leaders (KOLs) and Healthcare Professionals (HCPs) with which to develop professional relationships to ensure exchange of medical-scientific information relevant to CSL Seqirus’s products and areas of therapeutic interest. Gather, translate, and communicate actionable, strategy-aligned insights from scientific, educational, and conference setting interactions. Attend scientific and medical meetings. Deliver approved educational programs and training to relevant internal functions. Maintain excellent professional relationships, engage and cultivate relationships with leading KOLs to gain contribution/participation in advisory boards, greater understanding of influenza vaccines and insights into unmet patient needs. Represents CSL Seqirus at scientific and medical forums, including medical education forums, scientific roundtables, congresses, and symposia. Planning, designing, and managing or participating in local, regional, national, and global medical Advisory Boards including working with vendor(s) in support of medical affairs strategies.

rows.title: Senior AI Engineer I
rows.descriptionText:
About The Role

As a Senior AI Engineer I embedded within Secure Power, you leverage generative AI, automation platforms, and low-code tooling to solve real operational problems and remove manual work from the team’s day-to-day. You build, test, and deploy AI agents, automated workflows, and dashboards while maintaining the integrations and infrastructure that keep them running. Your core responsibilities include translating business rules and decision logic into reliable agent instructions, converting manual processes into automated workflows, and building the dashboards leadership relies on to track performance. You automate processes for Secure Power to enhance efficiency and collaborate with process owners and team leaders to develop working prototypes and production-ready tools.

Your mission is to apply specialized technical expertise in AI and automation to identify inefficiencies, map processes, and build new tools that address Secure Power’s most persistent operational pain points. Your work directly impacts how Secure Power runs day to day – contributing to faster cycle times, cleaner data, and better visibility for leadership. You are a specialized technical expert in AI engineering, focused on the delivery, implementation, and design of AI agents, automation, and reporting tools embedded within a single business team. You apply broad technical knowledge to deliver results with direct, visible impact on Secure Power’s operations. You make decisions regarding your own work and priorities, often guided by established precedents, technical standards, and some interpretation. You are responsible for guiding other professionals and providing mentorship on non-routine or escalated issues, and your work is reviewed for accuracy and quality to ensure the highest standards of AI engineering are met.

What You Will Do

Build and deploy AI agents (e.g., using Microsoft Copilot Studio) that solve real Secure Power business problems Design and maintain the automation and dashboard infrastructure (Power Automate, Power Apps, Power BI, Smartsheet) that supports scalable, production-grade solutions for the team. Collaborate with process owners and team leaders to map current-state workflows, redesign broken or redundant steps, and transform them into working prototypes and Minimum Viable Products (MVPs). Automate workflows and processes across systems the team already uses – including Salesforce, Oracle, CPQ, and SharePoint – to boost efficiency and remove manual re-entry. Run pilots, gather feedback, and iterate quickly; create simple documentation so the team can use and own what you’ve built. Collaborate with the central AI team and ensure all AI solutions adhere to established governance, security, and responsible AI policies. 

Required Skills

AI Agent Development: Building, training, and deploying AI agents (e.g., Copilot Studio) into real production use. Workflow Automation: Implementing and deploying automated workflows in low-code platforms (e.g., Power Automate, Power Apps). Process Mapping & Redesign: Mapping current-state workflows end-to-end and identifying where automation will – and won’t – add value. Data Integration: Connecting AI and automation tools across enterprise systems via API (e.g., Salesforce, Oracle) to eliminate manual data re-entry. Prompt & Logic Design: Translating business rules and decision logic into clear, testable agent instructions. Responsible AI & Governance: Applying data privacy, security, and responsible AI practices, including human review where outputs affect a customer or an order. 

Qualifications For Success

Strong problem-solving mindset with the ability to handle ambiguous, undocumented processes independently. Excellent collaboration skills with cross-functional teams to translate business requirements into technical solutions. Growth-oriented mindset with strong curiosity to explore new AI and automation technologies and methodologies. Adaptability to changing priorities and the ability to navigate a fast-moving, embedded team environment with ease. Comfortable explaining a technical tradeoff to a non-technical stakeholder or leader. 

Benefits & Growth

Collaborate with Secure Power leaders, process owners, and the central AI team in a supportive, innovation-driven culture. Access continuous learning opportunities, certifications, and technical mentorship

rows.title: Research Scientist, Lentiviral Vector Purification and Analytics
rows.descriptionText:
Summary

The Lentiviral Vector (LVV) Team in the Biologics Research Center (BRC) at Novartis, Cambridge, MA is seeking a highly motivated Research Scientist with experience in production and purification of viral vectors to join our team. In this role, you will play a key part in advancing our Cell and Gene Therapy research initiatives and contributing to groundbreaking research in CAR-T cell therapy.

About The Role

Internal Job Title: Research Scientist I/II

Position Location: Cambridge, MA, onsite

 This role is based in Cambridge, MA/USA. Novartis is unable to offer relocation support for this role: please only apply if this location is accessible for you.

Join a collaborative team at the forefront of cell and gene therapy research. As a Research Scientist focused on lentiviral vector purification and analytics, you will apply hands-on laboratory expertise to help develop, optimize, and characterize viral vector processes that support next-generation CAR-T programs. This role offers the opportunity to contribute directly to innovative science, work across purification and analytical workflows, and help advance high-quality research materials that enable transformative therapeutic approaches.

Key Responsibilities

This is a lab-based position that requires hands-on execution of activities related to lentiviral vector purification including clarification, chromatography and TFF.Execute analytical methods (molecular- and cell-based) to assess quality of the purified vector.Write and review protocols, technical reports, and technology transfer documents with supported conclusions and recommendations.Write and review SOPs, instrument procedures, and other lab documents.Plan and prioritize work to meet goals while managing multiple research activities.Support experimental design, data analysis, and troubleshooting.Identify root causes, implement solutions, and verify effectiveness.Present scientific data and contribute openly to discussions.Document experimental procedures and processes thoroughly.Collaborate across teams, share knowledge, and train team members in technical areas as needed.

Essential Requirements

BS or MS in bioengineering, virology, or related field, with relevant lab experience. This is not a PhD-level position.1–3 years of experience in protein and/or viral vector purification.Hands-on experience with chromatography and filtration techniques, including TFF and depth filtration.Strong coordination, communication, collaboration, learning agility, and self-motivation.Proficiency with Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and GraphPad Prism.Excellent oral, written, and interpersonal communication skills.

Desirable Requirements

BSL2 experience with AAV, lentiviral, or retroviral vector production.Proficiency in aseptic technique, cell culture, molecular biology, and analytical testing.Bioreactor experience.

The salary for this position is expected to range between $66,800 and $124,000 per year for Research Scientist I, and between $81,200 and $150,800 per year for Research Scientist II. The final salary offered is determined based on factors like, but not limited to, relevant skills and experience, and upon joining Novartis will be reviewed periodically. Your compensation will include a performance-based cash incentive and, depending on the level of the role, eligibility to be considered for annual equity awards.

US-based eligible employees will receive a comprehensive benefits package that includes health, life and disability benefits, a 401(k) with company contribution and match, and a variety of other benefits. In addition, employees are eligible for a generous time off package including vacation, personal days, holidays and other leaves.

rows.descriptionText:
About The Opportunity

About the Opportunity

Northeastern University Pharmaceutical Industry Fellowships Program is a two-year experiential program designed to advance lifelong learning and the education and training of Pharm.D. graduates. A key element of the program’s success is preparing Fellows to meet evolving workforce needs across various sectors of the pharmaceutical industry.

Fellows have the opportunity to work closely with our innovative biopharmaceutical industry partners, while engaging with Northeastern University faculty in professional and career development, teaching, service, and scholarly activities.

In partnership with Northeastern University, Intellia Therapeutics is offering a two-year Health economics and outcomes research (HEOR) fellowship, based in Cambridge, MA.

About Intellia

Intellia Therapeutics is a Cambridge-based biotechnology company focused on developing clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR)-based gene editing therapies to transform lives of people with severe diseases. In fact, Intellia’s co-founder Jennifer Doudna along with Emmanuelle Charpentier were awarded the 2020 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for their pioneering work in CRISPR.

At Intellia, we are humbled to contribute to what we believe to be medical history. As a leader in this field, our responsibility and commitment to patients is critical in our pursuit of developing novel, potentially curative therapeutics utilizing CRISPR-based technologies.

More specifically, we are employing a modular gene editing platform to create diverse in vivo and ex vivo therapeutics, spanning a range of disease indications. Guided by this full-spectrum approach, we are committed to making CRISPR-based medicines a reality for people living with genetic diseases and to creating novel engineered cell therapies for various cancers and autoimmune diseases.

Intellia HEOR Fellowship Program Overview

Northeastern University Pharmaceutical Industry Fellowships Program is a 2-year experiential program designed to advance lifelong learning and the education and training of PharmD/MPH/PhD graduates. A key element of the program’s success is preparing Fellows to meet evolving workforce needs across various sectors of the pharmaceutical industry. Fellows have the opportunity to work closely with our innovative biopharmaceutical industry partners, while engaging with Northeastern University faculty in professional and career development, teaching, service, and scholarly activities. In partnership with Northeastern University, Intellia Therapeutics is offering a 2-year Global HEOR and Evidence Strategy fellowship, based in Cambridge, MA.

What Sets the Intellia Fellowship Apart?

During the program, Fellows will work collaboratively and cross-functionally in Intellia’s HEOR and Evidence Strategy team, gaining exposure to our high-energy, fast-paced, and supportive culture. The HEOR and Evidence Strategy team sits within the Market Access and Patient Services team in the Commercial Organization. At Intellia, a technical and scientific expertise background is highly valued. The Fellowship offers a uniquely structured experience, beginning with a foundational year working with the Director, HEOR and Evidence Strategy supporting the HEOR strategy for Intellia’s novel, gene-editing therapies. This foundational year provides the Fellow with a strong understanding of strategic development of value and evidence generation strategy to support clinical development and commercial brand plans. In the second year, the Fellow will have an option to participate in 1-3 projects / activities within the broader Market Access and Patient Services team. These optional activities will aim to give the Fellow exposure to key strategic or execution activities that fall within Field HEOR and Market Access Strategy. rows.title: ML Engineer, Applied AI
rows.descriptionText:
Your Impact at LILA

We are growing our Applied AI org and seeking Machine Learning Engineers with expertise in model training, evaluation, and production-oriented ML systems. You’ll work on improving Lila’s AI models for customer-specific scientific needs, with a focus on turning frontier model capabilities into reliable workflows that can be evaluated, iterated, and used in real customer contexts. This is a rare chance to join an early team with the autonomy, flexibility, and compute to tackle frontier science problems.

Applied AI sits at the intersection of AI Research, model engineering, and product deployment. The team partners closely with AI Researchers and Software teams to adapt Lila models to customer workflows, improve model quality through experimentation, and ensure model behavior works well end to end inside the application.

This role is ideal for someone who can bridge research and engineering: training or adapting models, building evaluation loops, debugging model behavior, and collaborating across AI and Software to move promising capabilities into production-quality systems.

What You'll Be Building

Close the last-mile gap between Lila AI model capabilities and customer-specific scientific workflows.Post-train models using approaches such as SFT and RL (DPO, PPO/GRPO) to align model behavior with customer-specific requirements and feedback.Build evaluation loops that measure model quality, reliability, and customer fit.Design experiments to improve model performance across applied customer use cases.Feed customer learnings, data signals, and evaluation results back into the Lila AI model improvement cycles.Partner with AI researchers to translate model improvements into usable capabilities.Work with Software to integrate model behavior into end-to-end product workflows.Debug model failures using traces, evaluations, customer context, and scientific feedback.Build reusable tooling for model adaptation, evaluation, and deployment workflows.

What You'll Need To Succeed

Experience building, training, adapting, or evaluating machine learning models.Strong software engineering skills in Python and modern ML frameworks such as PyTorch, JAX, or TensorFlow.Experience designing experiments, evaluation metrics, or test sets for model performance.Ability to debug model behavior using data, traces, logs, and qualitative feedback.Experience working across research and engineering teams to move ML capabilities into usable systems.Familiarity with large language models, multi-modal models, or agentic AI systems.Clear communication skills for translating customer needs into technical model improvements.

Bonus Points For

Experience adapting models for customer-facing or production workflows.Experience with scientific, technical, or data-intensive customer use cases.Experience building evaluation harnesses, model monitoring, or quality dashboards.Familiarity with retrieval-augmented generation, tool use, or agentic workflows.Experience with RL post-training, such as RLHF, GRPO, or tool-augmented RL.Experience training MoE architectures.Experience working with product or customer-facing teams to translate needs into ML improvements.

CompensationWe offer competitive base compensation with bonus potential and generous early-stage equity. Your final offer will reflect your background, expertise, and expected impact.U.S. Benefits. Full-time U.S. employees receive a comprehensive benefits program including medical, dental, and vision coverage; employer-paid life and disability insurance; flexible time off with generous company wide holidays; paid parental leave; an educational assistance program; commuter benefits, including bike share memberships for office based employees; and a company subsidized lunch program.International Benefits. Full-time employees outside the U.S. receive a comprehensive benefits program tailored to their region. USD salary ranges apply only to U.S.-based positions; international salaries are set to local market.

Expected Base Salary Range: $116,000 USD - $170,000 USD

About LILA

Lila Sciences is building Scientific Superintelligence™ to solve humankind's greatest challenges. We believe science is the most inspiring frontier for AI. Rather than hard-coding expert knowledge into tools, LILA builds systems that can learn for themselves.

LILA combines advanced AI models with proprietary AI Science Factory™ instruments into an operating system for science that executes the entire scientific method autonomously, accelerating discovery at unprecedented speed, scale, and impact across medicine, materials, and energy. Learn more at www.lila.ai.

Guided by our core values of truth, trust, curiosity, grit, and velocity, we move with startup speed while tackling problems of historic importance. If this sounds like an environment you'd love to work in, even if you don't meet every qualification listed above, we encourage you to apply.

We’re All In

Lila Sciences is committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity or Veteran status.

Information you provide during your application process will be handled in accordance with our Candidate Privacy Policy.

A Note to Agencies

Lila Sciences does not accept unsolicited resumes from any source other than candidates. The submission of unsolicited resumes by recruitment or staffing agencies to Lila Sciences or its employees is strictly prohibited unless contacted directly by Lila Science’s internal Talent Acquisition team. rows.title: Scientist, Wet Lab Automation (On-site)
rows.descriptionText:
Job Description

Job Summary:

We are seeking a highly motivated Automation Scientist to join the Data, AI & Genome Sciences team at our Company Research Laboratories in Cambridge, MA. In this role, you will operate, maintain, and optimize advanced automation platforms and laboratory instrumentation to support drug discovery and development programs. The successful candidate will manage multiple projects, develop and improve automated workflows, analyze experimental results, troubleshoot system issues, and ensure reliable operation of automated systems. Experience with automated liquid handlers, laboratory robotics, and analytical instruments is required, along with strong attention to detail, problem-solving skills, and the ability to follow and validate scientific protocols in a fast-paced, innovative environment.

Responsibilities

Collaborate closely with experimental biologists, data analysts, and therapeutic area subject matter experts to develop and implement scalable automation workflows that enable high-quality, reproducible data generation in a timely manner. Design and execute large-scale automation protocols for cutting-edge single-cell and molecular assays (e.g., Parse-seq, 10x Flex, CROP-seq/Perturb-seq, Olink HT, immune profiling, Multiome ATAC-seq), high-throughput CRISPR screens, and complex 3D model generation using a variety of liquid handlers and robotic instruments. rows.descriptionText:
About The Opportunity

About the Opportunity

Northeastern University Pharmaceutical Industry Fellowships Program is a two-year experiential program designed to advance lifelong learning and the education and training of Pharm.D. graduates. A key element of the program’s success is preparing Fellows to meet evolving workforce needs across various sectors of the pharmaceutical industry.

Fellows have the opportunity to work closely with our innovative biopharmaceutical industry partners, while engaging with Northeastern University faculty in professional and career development, teaching, service, and scholarly activities.

In partnership with Northeastern University, Ironwood Pharmaceuticals is offering a two-year Medical Scientific Affairs fellowship, based in Boston, Massachusetts.

About Ironwood

Ironwood Pharmaceuticals (Nasdaq: IRWD), is a biotechnology company focused on developing and commercializing therapies for people living with gastrointestinal (GI) and rare diseases. Ironwood is advancing apraglutide, a next-generation, long-acting synthetic GLP-2 analog being developed for patients with short bowel syndrome who are dependent on parenteral support. Ironwood has also been a pioneer in the development of LINZESS® (linaclotide), the U.S. branded prescription market leader for adults with irritable bowel syndrome with constipation (IBS-C) or chronic idiopathic constipation (CIC) and pediatric patients with IBS-C or functional constipation (FC).

Founded in 1998, Ironwood is headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts, with additional operations in Basel, Switzerland.

Responsibilities

The Medical Scientific Affairs (MSA) fellowship is designed to provide the fellow with experience as an integrated member of the MSA team, contributing to strategic medical initiatives while developing competencies in core areas of MSA functions, such as Publications and Scientific Communications, Field Medical Affairs (Medical Science Liaison), Medical Information, Medical Education, and Evidence Generation.

The fellow will work closely with colleagues across MSA and other functional areas, including clinical development, regulatory, patient safety, commercial, data sciences, and legal. The fellow will also gain exposure to external partner interactions, vendor oversight, and opportunities to precept PharmD Co-Op students.

Job Duties

 Contribute to the development and maintenance of Ironwood Medical Scientific Affairs strategic plans. Work cross-functionally internally (commercial, medical writing, regulatory, legal, etc.) to provide subject matter expertise for medical strategy planning and content development. Collaborate cross-functionally to provide key MSA deliverables, such as the scientific communication platforms, publications strategy and medical communication strategy. Develop various types of internally or externally facing evidence-based medical content for symposia, training material and other MSA materials. Cross-functional collaboration to ensure strategic alignment, medical accuracy, evidence-based representation of Ironwood GI products in US and partnered regions. Generate medical insights from the perspectives of the patients and providers to support development of strategic plans. Participate in insight gathering activities Contribute to the maintenance of key medical information deliverables, including creation and updates FAQ documents and any required custom responses. Provide comprehensive training with respect to disease state(s) and product(s) and/or investigational agents to which fellow will be assigned. Participate in scientific congress, advisory committee, and KOL engagement activities. Precept PharmD students during their co-op and/or IPPE/APPE rotations. Participate in a rotational opportunity based on business needs, availability, and fellow interest. Additional responsibilities to be assigned based on individual interests.


The Successful Candidate Will Demonstrate

 PharmD from an accredited college or university before the start of the fellowship term; Ability to interpret and discuss complex medical scientific data; Excellent project management, time management and organizational skills; Ability to learn new skills and apply them broadly across MSA initiatives; Effective communication skills, both written and verbal; Record of medical and/or scientific publications preferred; Proactive individual capable of assessing needs, then creating solutions that effectively meet the need; Flexibility and ability to adapt quickly as company priorities change; Excellent interpersonal skills in order to effectively manage expectations and facilitate collaborative, working relationships; A positive attitude while adjusting to different personal approaches; Advanced proficiency and extensive experience with Microsoft Office Suite, such as Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, and Word;


Ironwood Pharmaceuticals is an equal opportunity employer welcoming diversity in our workforce.

Qualifications

 Doctor of Pharmacy degree from an ACPE-accredited institution Eligible for pharmacist licensure in the State of Massachusetts Excellent oral and written communication skills Strong time management and leadership abilities Ability to work independently and take initiative on a variety of projects at both the industry site and Northeastern Willingness and ability to relocate to Boston, Massachusetts before the Fellowship start date of July 1, 2027.


Additional Information

Applicants should submit the following application materials by the priority deadline of October 31, 2026:

 Curriculum vitae (CV), uploaded Unofficial PharmD transcripts, uploaded Cover letter, uploaded


Letters of Recommendation

Three formal Letters of Recommendation (LORs) must be submitted directly by the letter writers no later than November 23, 2026.

Each Letter Writer Must Include

About The Role

As a Senior AI Engineer I embedded within Secure Power, you leverage generative AI, automation platforms, and low-code tooling to solve real operational problems and remove manual work from the team’s day-to-day. You build, test, and deploy AI agents, automated workflows, and dashboards while maintaining the integrations and infrastructure that keep them running. Your core responsibilities include translating business rules and decision logic into reliable agent instructions, converting manual processes into automated workflows, and building the dashboards leadership relies on to track performance. You automate processes for Secure Power to enhance efficiency and collaborate with process owners and team leaders to develop working prototypes and production-ready tools.

Your mission is to apply specialized technical expertise in AI and automation to identify inefficiencies, map processes, and build new tools that address Secure Power’s most persistent operational pain points. Your work directly impacts how Secure Power runs day to day – contributing to faster cycle times, cleaner data, and better visibility for leadership. You are a specialized technical expert in AI engineering, focused on the delivery, implementation, and design of AI agents, automation, and reporting tools embedded within a single business team. You apply broad technical knowledge to deliver results with direct, visible impact on Secure Power’s operations. You make decisions regarding your own work and priorities, often guided by established precedents, technical standards, and some interpretation. You are responsible for guiding other professionals and providing mentorship on non-routine or escalated issues, and your work is reviewed for accuracy and quality to ensure the highest standards of AI engineering are met.

What You Will Do

Build and deploy AI agents (e.g., using Microsoft Copilot Studio) that solve real Secure Power business problems Design and maintain the automation and dashboard infrastructure (Power Automate, Power Apps, Power BI, Smartsheet) that supports scalable, production-grade solutions for the team. Collaborate with process owners and team leaders to map current-state workflows, redesign broken or redundant steps, and transform them into working prototypes and Minimum Viable Products (MVPs). Automate workflows and processes across systems the team already uses – including Salesforce, Oracle, CPQ, and SharePoint – to boost efficiency and remove manual re-entry. Run pilots, gather feedback, and iterate quickly; create simple documentation so the team can use and own what you’ve built. Process Mapping & Redesign: Mapping current-state workflows end-to-end and identifying where automation will – and won’t – add value. Data Integration: Connecting AI and automation tools across enterprise systems via API (e.g., Salesforce, Oracle) to eliminate manual data re-entry. Prompt & Logic Design: Translating business rules and decision logic into clear, testable agent instructions. Responsible AI & Governance: Applying data privacy, security, and responsible AI practices, including human review where outputs affect a customer or an order.

Strong problem-solving mindset with the ability to handle ambiguous, undocumented processes independently. Excellent collaboration skills with cross-functional teams to translate business requirements into technical solutions. Growth-oriented mindset with strong curiosity to explore new AI and automation technologies and methodologies. Adaptability to changing priorities and the ability to navigate a fast-moving, embedded team environment with ease. Comfortable explaining a technical tradeoff to a non-technical stakeholder or leader.

Full-time Co-op (≥6 months)

 In person Boston, MA (Seaport)

About Kernal Biologics, Inc.

Kernal Bio is a venture-backed therapeutics company engineering cells inside the body using AI-designed, selective mRNA and targeted LNP technology. By developing in vivo CAR-T therapies, Kernal Bio is advancing precision treatments for autoimmune diseases and blood cancers. The company was founded by experts from MIT, Harvard, Merck, and BMS, and its leadership team brings a track record of three FDA-approved therapies and over 120 patents. With support from leading investors, including Hummingbird Ventures, Amgen Ventures, Y Combinator, and HBM, Kernal Bio is transforming the future of cell therapy design and delivery.

Job Summary

We are seeking a highly motivated researcher to fill a Co-op position on our Synthetic Biology team, supporting the design, production, and in vitro testing of mRNA therapeutics. This is a hands-on, bench-based role: you will work with mammalian cell lines every day, transfect and test mRNAs, and support DNA template and mRNA production, while learning cutting-edge mRNA and synthetic biology technologies as an integral member of the team. You will perform experimental research, document it, and present your results.

Key Responsibilities

In partnership with Northeastern University, Intellia Therapeutics is offering a two-year Health economics and outcomes research (HEOR) fellowship, based in Cambridge, MA.

About Intellia

Intellia Therapeutics is a Cambridge-based biotechnology company focused on developing clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR)-based gene editing therapies to transform lives of people with severe diseases. In fact, Intellia’s co-founder Jennifer Doudna along with Emmanuelle Charpentier were awarded the 2020 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for their pioneering work in CRISPR.

At Intellia, we are humbled to contribute to what we believe to be medical history. As a leader in this field, our responsibility and commitment to patients is critical in our pursuit of developing novel, potentially curative therapeutics utilizing CRISPR-based technologies.

More specifically, we are employing a modular gene editing platform to create diverse in vivo and ex vivo therapeutics, spanning a range of disease indications. Guided by this full-spectrum approach, we are committed to making CRISPR-based medicines a reality for people living with genetic diseases and to creating novel engineered cell therapies for various cancers and autoimmune diseases.

Intellia HEOR Fellowship Program Overview

Northeastern University Pharmaceutical Industry Fellowships Program is a 2-year experiential program designed to advance lifelong learning and the education and training of PharmD/MPH/PhD graduates. rows.descriptionText:
Summary

The Lentiviral Vector (LVV) Team in the Biologics Research Center (BRC) at Novartis, Cambridge, MA is seeking a highly motivated Research Scientist with experience in production and purification of viral vectors to join our team. In this role, you will play a key part in advancing our Cell and Gene Therapy research initiatives and contributing to groundbreaking research in CAR-T cell therapy.

About The Role

Internal Job Title: Research Scientist I/II

Position Location: Cambridge, MA, onsite

 This role is based in Cambridge, MA/USA. Novartis is unable to offer relocation support for this role: please only apply if this location is accessible for you.

Join a collaborative team at the forefront of cell and gene therapy research. As a Research Scientist focused on lentiviral vector purification and analytics, you will apply hands-on laboratory expertise to help develop, optimize, and characterize viral vector processes that support next-generation CAR-T programs. This role offers the opportunity to contribute directly to innovative science, work across purification and analytical workflows, and help advance high-quality research materials that enable transformative therapeutic approaches.

Key Responsibilities

This is a lab-based position that requires hands-on execution of activities related to lentiviral vector purification including clarification, chromatography and TFF.Execute analytical methods (molecular- and cell-based) to assess quality of the purified vector.Write and review protocols, technical reports, and technology transfer documents with supported conclusions and recommendations.Write and review SOPs, instrument procedures, and other lab documents.Plan and prioritize work to meet goals while managing multiple research activities.Support experimental design, data analysis, and troubleshooting.Identify root causes, implement solutions, and verify effectiveness.Present scientific data and contribute openly to discussions.Document experimental procedures and processes thoroughly.Collaborate across teams, share knowledge, and train team members in technical areas as needed.

Essential Requirements

BS or MS in bioengineering, virology, or related field, with relevant lab experience. This is not a PhD-level position.1–3 years of experience in protein and/or viral vector purification.Hands-on experience with chromatography and filtration techniques, including TFF and depth filtration.Strong coordination, communication, collaboration, learning agility, and self-motivation.Proficiency with Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and GraphPad Prism.Excellent oral, written, and interpersonal communication skills.

Desirable Requirements

BSL2 experience with AAV, lentiviral, or retroviral vector production.Proficiency in aseptic technique, cell culture, molecular biology, and analytical testing.Bioreactor experience.

The salary for this position is expected to range between $66,800 and $124,000 per year for Research Scientist I, and between $81,200 and $150,800 per year for Research Scientist II. The final salary offered is determined based on factors like, but not limited to, relevant skills and experience, and upon joining Novartis will be reviewed periodically. Novartis may change the published salary range based on company and market factors.

Your compensation will include a performance-based cash incentive and, depending on the level of the role, eligibility to be considered for annual equity awards.

US-based eligible employees will receive a comprehensive benefits package that includes health, life and disability benefits, a 401(k) with company contribution and match, and a variety of other benefits. In addition, employees are eligible for a generous time off package including vacation, personal days, holidays and other leaves.
